name: Qwen3.8-27B / Qwen3.6-27B (dense hybrid, 262K ctx): default pick for 24 GB cards
what: Dense 27B models from Alibaba with a hybrid layout: 3 Gated DeltaNet (linear attention) layers for every 1 full-attention layer. Only 16 of the 64 layers keep a KV cache, so long context costs much less memory than on a classic 27-32B model. Both accept image input, think by default, use Apache 2.0, and currently report the best agentic-coding scores that fit on one 24 GB GPU.
date: Qwen3.6-27B: 2026-04-22; Qwen3.8-27B: 2026-08-14 (per QwenLM README News)
concrete_claims: Release dates: Qwen3.8-27B on 2026-08-14, Qwen3.6-27B on 2026-04-22, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 2026-04-16 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.6/main/README.md). Qwen3.6-27B architecture: 64 layers, hidden 5120, layout 16 x (3 x Gated DeltaNet -> 1 x Gated Attention), 24 Q heads, 4 KV heads, head_dim 256 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, as quoted in search results). Qwen3.8-27B uses the same architecture (https://dev.to/jamilxt/qwen-38-27b-vs-qwen-36-27b-same-architecture-4-months-apart-and-a-different-kind-of-upgrade-3280). Qwen3.6-27B vendor scores: SWE-bench Verified 77.2, SWE-bench Pro 53.5, Terminal-Bench 2.0 59.3, measured on an internal scaffold at temp 1.0 with 200K context (https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.6-27b); BenchLM also lists TB2.0 at 59.3 (https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2). Qwen3.8-27B card: SWE-bench Pro 61.7 with Qwen's own task set and the Claude Code harness, QwenSWEBench 79.0, native context 262,144 tokens extensible to 1M with YaRN (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B). Ollama tag `qwen3.8:27b` is 27.3B parameters, Q4_K_M, about 18 GB, with vision, tools and thinking (https://ollama.com/library/qwen3.8:27b). Ollama added Qwen 3.8 support in the v0.34 line; v0.34.4 shipped 2026-09-23 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.34.4). Qwen3.6 thinking-mode sampling for coding: temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, min_p=0, presence_penalty=0 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). Official serving flags: `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.6/main/README.md). Qwen3.8 adds `reasoning_effort` and `preserve_thinking` (same README). Community guides say the default effort is xhigh, which costs a lot of wall-clock time on a single GPU (https://kingy.ai/blog/qwen3-8-27b-local-coding-agent/, https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/run-qwen3-8-27b-locally-reasoning-effort). Measured on an RTX 4090 with Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M in llama.cpp: about 38 tok/s at 256K context with q4 KV in about 22 GB VRAM, and about 38.6 tok/s at 64K (https://github.com/outsourc-e/qwen36-4090-recipes, 2026-04-25).
how_we_use_it: Make this the recommended default in the model picker (SettingsPanel.tsx) when gpu_stats() in src-tauri/src/system.rs reports at least 20 GB total VRAM: `qwen3.8:27b`, with `qwen3.6:27b` as the fallback if the user's Ollama is older than v0.34. On first use, call the existing ollama_create_variant (src-tauri/src/ollama.rs) to create something like `qwen3.8-27b-cw64k` with num_ctx 65536, or 131072 when KV is q8_0, and write that tag into CodeWhale's [providers.ollama] model. For local models, set a per-model reasoning_effort preset of 'medium', or 'low' for quick edits, instead of CodeWhale's example 'max' (config.example.toml), because Ollama's OpenAI layer passes reasoning_effort through (docs/api/openai-compatibility.mdx). Ship the coding sampling preset (temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20) as Modelfile parameters on the same variant. For the Godot shader loop, the long context means the skill, the shader file and the compiler errors fit in one turn.

name: VRAM fit estimator: weights plus a KV cache formula that understands hybrid, SWA and GQA layouts
what: A per-GPU recommender that adds three terms: weight bytes (params x bits-per-weight / 8), KV bytes (2 x attention layers that grow a cache x KV heads x head_dim x bytes per element x context x parallel), and fixed overhead. The architecture numbers come from the GGUF metadata that Ollama already returns from /api/show, and the result is checked against /api/ps after loading.
date: Formula is standard; GGUF keys checked against llama.cpp master and Ollama docs on 2026-10-13
concrete_claims: KV formula: 2 x layers x KV heads x head_dim x seq_len x bytes per element, times batch size. Sliding-window and hybrid architectures count only the layers that actually grow a cache, and MLA uses a compressed latent instead (https://sebastianraschka.com/llm-architecture-gallery/kv-cache-calculations, https://www.morphllm.com/kv-cache-explained). Bits per weight measured by llama.cpp: Q4_K_M 4.8944, Q5_K_M 5.7036, Q6_K 6.5633, Q8_0 8.5008, IQ4_XS 4.4597, Q3_K_M 3.9960 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/tools/quantize/README.md). GGUF metadata keys: `%s.attention.head_count_kv`, `%s.attention.key_length`, `%s.attention.value_length`, `%s.attention.sliding_window`, `%s.attention.sliding_window_pattern`, `%s.full_attention_interval` (qwen35/qwen3next), `%s.ssm.*` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/src/llama-arch.cpp). /api/show returns `model_info` with `<arch>.block_count`, `<arch>.attention.head_count_kv`, `<arch>.context_length`, and `capabilities` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/api.md). /api/ps returns `size`, `size_vram` and `context_length` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/api/types.go). Ollama KV types: q8_0 uses about half the memory of f16 and q4_0 about a quarter (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/faq.mdx). Required RAM scales with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL x OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH (same FAQ). llama.cpp's `llama-fit-params` / `--fit` estimates projected device memory, defaults to a 1024 MiB margin, and prints fitted `-c`, `-ngl` and `-ot` arguments (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/tools/fit-params/README.md). Worked f16 KV per token, computed from the published configs: Qwen3.6/3.8-27B = 2x16x4x256x2 B = 64 KiB (16 GiB at 262,144 tokens; about 4.5 GiB with q4_0); Qwen3.6-35B-A3B = 2x10x2x256x2 B = 20 KiB, with 40 layers, 10 of them full attention and 2 KV heads (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B); Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B = 2x48x4x128x2 B = 96 KiB; gpt-oss-20b = 12 full-attention layers x 8 KV heads x head_dim 64, about 24 KiB, with the other 12 layers on a 128-token sliding window (https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-20b/blob/main/config.json); Devstral Small 2 = 40 layers x 8 KV heads x 128, so 160 KiB per token (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512/blob/main/config.json). Cross-check: the measured 22 GB for Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M at 256K with q4 KV (https://github.com/outsourc-e/qwen36-4090-recipes) is consistent with about 16.7 GB of weights plus about 4.5 GiB of KV.
how_we_use_it: Add a Rust function, for example `estimate_fit(model_info, quant, ctx, kv_type, parallel)`, in src-tauri/src/ollama.rs. It reads `general.parameter_count`, `<arch>.block_count`, `head_count_kv` (scalar or per-layer array), `key_length`/`value_length`, `sliding_window`/`sliding_window_pattern`, `full_attention_interval` and `ssm.*` from the /api/show response the app already fetches. Combine that with `memTotalMb` from gpu_stats() (system.rs), keeping about 1 GiB of margin plus Windows/DWM usage. The UI shows a fit badge for each installed model and each catalog model (Fits at 64K / Fits at 128K with q8 KV / Spills to CPU) and offers a context slider that feeds ollama_create_variant. After loading, compare /api/ps `size_vram` with `size` to detect CPU spill and show a StatusBar warning. Optional power-user mode: locate the GGUF blob from the `FROM` line in /api/show `modelfile` and run a bundled `llama-fit-params` for an exact projection.

name: Ollama context and KV-cache configuration: avoid the silent 4K-context trap
what: Ollama now picks its default context from VRAM size, and that default is 4K on any GPU under 24 GiB. CodeWhale talks to Ollama through the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint, which cannot set num_ctx, so an untouched 8-16 GB setup runs agentic coding with a 4K window and silently truncates the prompt.
date: Ollama docs (main) read 2026-10-13; Ollama v0.34.4 = 2026-09-23
concrete_claims: Ollama's context-length doc: '< 24 GiB VRAM: 4k context; 24-48 GiB: 32k; >= 48 GiB: 256k'. Tasks such as 'agents, and coding tools should be set to at least 64000 tokens'. The doc gives `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve`, and `ollama ps` shows a CONTEXT column (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/context-length.mdx). OpenAI-compat doc: 'The OpenAI API does not have a way of setting the context size'; it says to create a model with `PARAMETER num_ctx` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/api/openai-compatibility.mdx). /api/create accepts `from` plus a `parameters` dictionary (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/api.md). KV quantization: `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE` defaults to f16; q8_0 is 'recommended if not using f16' and requires Flash Attention, which Ollama enables automatically when supported (`OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION`). `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` defaults to 1 and memory scales with NUM_PARALLEL x CONTEXT_LENGTH (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/faq.mdx). The OpenAI layer supports `reasoning_effort`; for models with named levels, unsupported names resolve to the model's default (openai-compatibility.mdx). Third-party reports confirm the 4K default for Gemma 4 (https://www.verdent.ai/guides/gemma-4-ollama).
how_we_use_it: The app already has ollama_create_variant (which bakes num_ctx, range 2048..262144) and reads `num_ctx` from /api/show parameters (ollama.rs). Turn this into a guarded flow. (1) Before starting the CodeWhale sidecar, if the selected model has no baked num_ctx and VRAM is under 24 GiB, block with a one-click 'Create 64K variant' or the estimator's best context. (2) If the desktop app manages the Ollama service, set OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1 and OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 at launch, and show them in the Inspector. (3) Poll /api/ps `context_length` and show the effective context in StatusBar.tsx next to the model name, in red when it is below 32K. (4) Map CodeWhale's reasoning tier to model-supported reasoning_effort names, read from /api/show, so 'max' does not quietly turn into the slowest setting on a local GPU.

name: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, about 3B active): fast agentic coder for 16-24 GB, with expert offload
what: A 35B-total mixture-of-experts model (256 experts, 8 routed plus 1 shared, about 3B active) on the same hybrid DeltaNet/attention base. Its KV cache is very small (2 KV heads on 10 attention layers) and it decodes much faster than the dense 27B. On 16 GB cards it remains usable by keeping some expert weights in system RAM.
concrete_claims: Architecture: 40 layers, layout 10 x (3 x Gated DeltaNet + MoE -> 1 x Gated Attention + MoE), 16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head_dim 256, 256 experts with 8 routed + 1 shared (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). Vendor scores: SWE-bench Verified 73.4, Terminal-Bench 2.0 51.5, SWE-bench Pro 49.5 on Qwen's internal scaffold (https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.6-35b-a3b, https://www.buildfastwithai.com/blogs/qwen3-6-35b-a3b-review). NVIDIA ran it in its own harness: SWE-bench Verified 70.12, Terminal-Bench 2.1 44.38 (https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nim/nvidia/models/nemotron-3.5-lightning/-, https://aireiter.com/blog/nemotron-3-5-lightning-guide). MCPMark 37.0, against 18.1 for Gemma4-31B and 14.2 for Gemma4-26B-A4B; measured with GitHub MCP v0.30.3 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). Ollama tags reported: `qwen3.6:35b-a3b` (Q4_K_M, about 22-24 GB) and `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-q8_0` (https://insiderllm.com/guides/qwen35-local-guide-which-model-fits-your-gpu/, https://tinyweights.dev/posts/run-qwen3-6-35b-a3b-locally/). llama.cpp `--n-cpu-moe N` keeps the expert weights of the first N layers on the CPU; `--cpu-moe` keeps all of them; `--moe-cache-mib` adds a GPU cache for CPU-resident experts (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/common/arg.cpp). Ollama has no per-model n-cpu-moe setting; feature request #11772 is open (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/11772). Estimates for a 16 GB RTX 5060 Ti: 31-53 tok/s at 32K with --n-cpu-moe 13; the author says these are bandwidth estimates, not measurements (https://dev.to/donald_lee_707b59c456e304/how-to-pick-n-cpu-moe-in-llamacpp-qwen36-35b-a3b-on-12-16-and-24-gb-gpus-43f3).
how_we_use_it: In the model catalog, offer it as the 'Fast' alternative to the 27B on 24 GB cards: lower peak quality, but much quicker turns in the shader compile-fix loop. Because KV is about 20 KiB per token, a 128K-context variant adds only about 2.5 GiB. On 16 GB cards, show it as 'Runs with CPU expert offload' only when the estimator finds at least 32 GB of free system RAM, and use the optional llama-server backend (see the llama.cpp item) with an auto-chosen --n-cpu-moe. If the user stays on Ollama, warn when /api/ps size_vram is less than size, because Ollama spills whole layers.

name: Tool-call reliability guardrails for Qwen-family models on Ollama (strict XML parser failures)
what: Qwen3.x tool calls are an XML-like format that Ollama converts and then parses with Go's strict xml.Unmarshal. There are open reports of intermittent HTTP 500s, and of deterministic failures on long file-write tool calls, where the parse error comes back to the client as the assistant's answer. A coding agent that writes whole shader files is the riskiest case.
date: Issues filed 2026; parser code read from ollama main 2026-10-13
concrete_claims: Ollama maps parser names `qwen3.5` -> Qwen35Parser and `qwen3-coder` -> Qwen3CoderParser (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/model/parsers/parsers.go). The Qwen3Coder parser runs `transformToXML(raw)` and then `xml.Unmarshal` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/model/parsers/qwen3coder.go). Issue #16383 reports that qwen3.6 tags register PARSER qwen3.5 and that Ollama intermittently returns 500 when the model drifts from its template (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/16383). Issue #18563 reports that the strict XML step 'rejects long file-write tool calls ... deterministically, and the client gets the error as the answer'; related PR #18571 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/18563). Issue #17276 reports intermittent failures in longer multi-step sessions (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/17276). For GLM-4.7-Flash, Unsloth advised against Ollama because of chat-template issues (https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/tutorials/glm-4.7-flash); Ollama now ships a dedicated `glm-4.7` parser (parsers.go). gpt-oss Harmony has a known problem with parallel tool calls in BFCL-style tests (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.07731). Mistral recommends temperature below 0.1 and a small tool set for Ministral 3 (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512).
how_we_use_it: On the desktop side, the event stream from the CodeWhale sidecar should flag an assistant message that contains an Ollama parse error (for example 'closed by', 'unmarshal', or HTTP 500 from /v1/chat/completions). Show a 'Tool-call parse failure' chip with an automatic retry that adds an instruction to use the patch/edit tool or write in chunks of no more than about 200 lines. Count failures per model in local settings and show them on the model card. Add a 'Tool-call reliability' smoke test (see the acceptance-test item) that runs a 400-line file write through the real toolset before a model is marked 'Agent-ready'. Pin the minimum Ollama version per model family in the catalog (for example qwen3.8 needs the v0.34 line), checked via /api/version, which ollama_status already reads.

name: Devstral Small 2 (24B dense, Mistral): strong agentic alternative, but KV-heavy
what: Mistral's 24B agentic coding model under Apache 2.0, with 256K context and native tool use, trained for SWE-style scaffolds. It is a good second opinion next to the Qwen models. It uses conventional full attention on all 40 layers with 8 KV heads, so long context is far more expensive than on Qwen3.6/3.8.
date: 2025-12-09 (Devstral 2 / Devstral Small 2 release); Mistral API now lists it as deprecated
concrete_claims: Released 2025-12-09 as Devstral 2 (123B) and Devstral Small 2 (24B), both with 256K context; Small 2 is Apache 2.0 (https://localaimaster.com/models/devstral, https://serenitiesai.com/articles/mistral-magistral-devstral-2-review-2026). SWE-bench Verified 68.0% and SWE-bench Multilingual 55.7% per Mistral, as listed on the Ollama page (https://dev.to/jangwook_kim_e31e7291ad98/devstral-2-run-mistrals-open-coding-agent-locally-13o). Ollama tag `devstral-small-2`, Q4_K_M about 15 GB (https://codersera.com/blog/run-devstral-locally-with-ollama/, https://www.canirun.ai/model/devstral-small-2-24b/). Config: text_config `ministral3`, hidden 5120, 40 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128 (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512/blob/main/config.json), which gives 160 KiB of f16 KV per token (my calculation). Mistral's API docs list Devstral Small 2 as deprecated in favor of Mistral Medium 3.5; the weights stay available (https://docs.mistral.ai/models). No new Devstral had been released in 2026 as of these sources.
how_we_use_it: List it in the catalog as 'Alternative agent (Mistral)' for 24 GB GPUs. The estimator should cap the default variant at about 48K with f16 KV, or about 90K with q8_0 KV, on 24 GB; the context slider should explain why, since 64K f16 KV alone is 10 GiB. Use a low default temperature (0.15 or less) for this family. Mark it 'no upstream updates expected' because of the API deprecation, so users are steered toward Qwen3.8 and then Devstral as a fallback when Qwen tool-call parsing misbehaves.

name: gpt-oss-20b (21B MoE, MXFP4): best fit for 16 GB cards
what: OpenAI's open-weight reasoning MoE. It natively ships with MXFP4 expert weights and fits in 16 GB, alternates 128-token sliding-window and full-attention layers (small KV), and has adjustable reasoning effort. It is solid for 16 GB GPUs, though uniform-harness results put it well behind the Qwen3.6 MoE on agentic coding.
date: August 2025 (no successor found as of Oct 2026)
concrete_claims: gpt-oss-20b requires only 16 GB of memory (https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-oss/). The Ollama download is about 14 GB; Ollama lists native function calling and structured outputs (https://ollama.com/library/gpt-oss). Config: 24 layers, 8 KV heads, sliding_window 128, `layer_types` alternating sliding/full (https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-20b/blob/main/config.json); head_dim 64 per the Transformers GptOss docs (https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/gpt_oss). In NVIDIA's single-harness comparison: SWE-bench Verified 52.44 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 15.17, against 70.12 and 44.38 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (https://aireiter.com/blog/nemotron-3-5-lightning-guide, https://kingy.ai/blog/nemotron-3-5-lightning-review/). The often-cited 60.7% SWE-bench Verified at high effort is from secondary summaries (https://www.morphllm.com/gpt-oss); I could not verify it against the model card PDF (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.10925). Ollama maps reasoning_effort for GPT-OSS: 'minimal' -> 'low', 'xhigh'/'ultra' -> 'high' (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/api/openai-compatibility.mdx). Harmony has a known parallel-tool-call problem in BFCL tests (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.07731). No gpt-oss successor or 2026 update was found (https://willitrunai.com/blog/gpt-oss-20b-vram-requirements).
how_we_use_it: Make it the default recommendation when gpu_stats reports 14-20 GB of VRAM: `gpt-oss:20b` with a 64K or 128K variant (KV is about 24 KiB per token, so 128K is about 3 GiB). Map CodeWhale's reasoning tiers to low/medium/high. In the sidecar config for this model, force parallel_tool_calls off or serialize calls to avoid the Harmony parallel-call weakness. Label it 'Good / fast on 16 GB' rather than 'Best', and suggest Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with offload when the user has more than 32 GB of system RAM.

name: Gemma 4 family (E2B / E4B / 26B-A4B MoE / 31B dense): multimodal all-rounder with native function calling
what: Google's Apache-2.0 family, released April 2026, with native function calling, structured JSON and system instructions. The 26B-A4B MoE (3.8B active) is a fast general model for 16-24 GB; E4B suits 8 GB. In third-party agentic tool-use tables it trails Qwen3.6, so it fits best as a general or vision helper rather than the main coding agent.
concrete_claims: Released April 2, 2026 under Apache 2.0 in E2B, E4B, 26B MoE and 31B Dense sizes, with native function calling and structured JSON; edge models have 128K context and larger ones up to 256K (https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemma-4/). The 26B-A4B has 25.2B total and 3.8B active parameters; the 31B has 30.7B with 256K context (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.05250 citing the model card). Ollama tags include e2b, e4b, 26b and 31b, with tools and thinking (https://registry.ollama.ai/library/gemma4). Q4 sizes: 26B about 16-18 GB, 31B about 19-20 GB (https://jacar.es/en/gemma-4-locally-with-ollama/). In NVIDIA's harness, 26B-A4B scored SWE-bench Verified 57.40 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 37.22 (https://aireiter.com/blog/nemotron-3-5-lightning-guide). Qwen's table: MCPMark 14.2 for 26B-A4B and 18.1 for 31B (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). Vendor τ²-bench is 76.9 for the 31B (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.05250). The Ollama context-length doc's example shows `gemma4:latest` at 131072 context, 9.6 GB, 100% GPU (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/context-length.mdx). llama.cpp has a `gemma4-assistant` architecture (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/src/llama-arch.cpp).
how_we_use_it: Catalog roles: `gemma4:e4b` is the 8 GB 'chat/explain' model and an image-understanding helper, for example reading a screenshot of a Godot shader artifact via read_image_b64 in system.rs. `gemma4:26b` is a 16-24 GB general model. Do not label Gemma 4 'Agent-ready' unless it passes the in-app tool-call smoke test. Always create a context variant, because the VRAM-tier default is 4K under 24 GiB.

name: GLM-4.7-Flash (30B-A3B MoE, about 200K ctx): strongest small GLM, with a template caveat
what: Z.ai's 30B-A3B open-weight model. Its vendor-reported SWE-bench Verified and τ²-Bench scores are strong for its size. Every GLM-5.x release since is far too large for local use (GLM-5.3-Flash is 320B-A18B), so this remains the GLM option for 8-24 GB.
date: January 2026
concrete_claims: SWE-bench Verified 59.2, against 22.0 for Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 and 34.0 for GPT-OSS-20B in Z.ai's table; τ²-Bench 79.5 (https://ollama.com/library/glm-4.7-flash, https://llm-stats.com/blog/research/glm-4.7-flash-launch). Ollama tag `glm-4.7-flash` is 19 GB with 198K context, and the readme says it requires Ollama 0.14.3 (https://ollama.com/library/glm-4.7-flash). Early users reported template problems with GGUF on Ollama (https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/tutorials/glm-4.7-flash, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46679872); current Ollama has a dedicated `glm-4.7` parser (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/model/parsers/parsers.go). GLM-5.3-Flash is 320B total / 18B active (https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/glm-5-3-flash-open-weight-model), and GLM-5.2 is about 753B (https://www.morphllm.com/glm-5-2); neither is local-feasible.
how_we_use_it: Add it as a 24 GB catalog entry: 'Alternative MoE, use only the official library tag, not community GGUFs'. The catalog should enforce the official tag because the parser is attached to it, while third-party GGUF imports may lack the right template. Run it through the tool-call smoke test on first install. Reasonable choice for users who want a non-Qwen MoE.

name: 8-12 GB tier: Qwen3.5-9B, Ministral 3 (8B/14B), Gemma 4 E4B
what: On smaller GPUs, current 8-14B models with native tool calling now replace the old deepseek-r1 distills and qwen3-4b. Qwen3.5-9B has the strongest vendor tool-use numbers; Ministral 3 14B is the largest that fits 12 GB with room for context.
concrete_claims: Qwen3.5-9B/4B/2B/0.8B were released on 2026-03-02 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.6/main/README.md). Qwen3.5-9B card: BFCL-V4 66.1 and TAU2-Bench 79.1 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B). It is about 5.5 GB at Q4_K_M and about 9.6 GB at Q8_0 (https://willitrunai.com/blog/qwen-3-5-9b-vram-requirements). Independent indices rate its agentic and coding ability much lower than the vendor numbers (https://apxml.com/models/qwen35-9b). Ministral 3 is 3B/8B/14B with native tool use, 256K context and Apache 2.0; Ollama `ministral-3:14b`; downloads about 6.0 GB (8B) and 9.1 GB (14B); Mistral recommends temperature below 0.1 and a small tool set (https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512, https://tinyweights.dev/posts/run-ministral-3-locally/). Ollama has a dedicated `ministral` parser (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/model/parsers/parsers.go). Gemma 4 E4B has 128K context and native function calling (https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemma-4/). Qwen3.5-4B shares Qwen3.6-27B's tokenizer (vocab 248,320) and works as a same-vocab draft model (https://github.com/outsourc-e/qwen36-4090-recipes).
how_we_use_it: When gpu_stats reports 12 GB or less, the onboarding recommender offers `qwen3.5:9b` (default, 32K-64K variant), `ministral-3:14b` on 12 GB, and `gemma4:e4b`. It sets honest expectations ('small edits, single-file shader fixes; multi-file refactors may fail'). If the user has qwen3-4b-32k installed, show an inline 'upgrade available' card. For the Godot workflow, pair the small model with a tighter loop (shorter skill prompt, compile-check after every edit) and route long multi-file tasks to a cloud provider that CodeWhale already supports, if the user opts in.

name: Benchmark hygiene plus a built-in local acceptance test per model
what: Public numbers for local models are mostly vendor-run on custom scaffolds, SWE-bench Verified is officially deprecated as saturated and contaminated, and the Aider polyglot leaderboard is stale. The most reliable signal is a small, quality-checked test run on the user's own GPU, through CodeWhale's real tools and the same Ollama path.
date: OpenAI deprecation: Feb 2026; Aider leaderboard last entry 2025-10-03; checked 2026-10-13
concrete_claims: OpenAI no longer reports SWE-bench Verified ('saturated', 'contamination') and recommends SWE-bench Pro (https://openai.com/index/why-we-no-longer-evaluate-swe-bench-verified/). Qwen's SWE-bench numbers come from an internal scaffold (https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.6-27b), and Qwen3.8's SWE-bench Pro from its own task set with the Claude Code harness (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B). The same model can score very differently by harness, for example GPT-5.5 at 83.1% in Codex against 78.0% in Terminus 2 on TB2 (https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2). NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning card gives a single-harness comparison of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma 4 26B-A4B and gpt-oss-20b (https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4). The Aider polyglot leaderboard's newest entries are dated 2025-10-03 (DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp); small-model rows include Qwen3 32B at 40.0% and gpt-oss-120b (high) at 41.8% (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aider-AI/aider/main/aider/website/_data/polyglot_leaderboard.yml). A useful design: per-category checks (list, code, json, reason, tool-call, essay) catch cases where the aggregate looks good but structured output is broken (https://github.com/outsourc-e/qwen36-4090-recipes).
how_we_use_it: Add a 'Qualify model' action to the model menu (CommandPalette.tsx and SettingsPanel.tsx) that runs 6-8 short scripted tasks through the CodeWhale sidecar against the chosen Ollama variant: valid JSON tool call, multi-tool sequence, a 300-400 line file write through the edit tool (catches the parser bug), a read-search-patch on a fixture repo, and a Godot task (fix a deliberately broken .gdshader until the existing compile-check passes). Record pass/fail, tokens per second (from Ollama's eval_count/eval_duration), time-to-first-token and peak VRAM. Show an 'Agent-ready' badge and a per-model scorecard. In the catalog, show vendor benchmarks with a 'vendor scaffold' label, prefer SWE-bench Pro / Terminal-Bench 2.x and uniform-harness numbers, and drop Aider polyglot from model cards.

name: Optional llama.cpp (llama-server) backend: --fit, MoE expert offload, same-vocab speculative decoding
what: Mainline llama.cpp now auto-fits context and layers to free VRAM, can keep only MoE expert weights in system RAM, can cache hot experts on the GPU, and supports draft-model and MTP speculative decoding. These are the main features Ollama does not expose per model, and they matter most on 12-16 GB GPUs and for MoE models.
date: llama.cpp master as of 2026-10-13; spec-dec measurements 2026-04-25
concrete_claims: `-fit/--fit [on|off]` adjusts unset arguments to fit device memory; `-fitt/--fit-target` sets the per-device margin; `-fitc/--fit-ctx` sets the minimum context; `-cmoe/--cpu-moe` and `-ncmoe/--n-cpu-moe N` (env LLAMA_ARG_N_CPU_MOE) keep expert weights on the CPU; `--moe-cache-mib N` is a GPU cache for CPU-resident experts; `--mtp` downloads multi-token-prediction heads (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/common/arg.cpp). `llama-fit-params` prints fitted `-c -ngl -ot` arguments and a memory breakdown (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/tools/fit-params/README.md). Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M on an RTX 4090 with mainline llama.cpp and a Qwen3.5-4B same-vocab draft: 43.2 tok/s mean and 67.1 peak at 8K, 6/6 quality checks passed; cross-vocab drafts (ik_llama.cpp with Qwen3-1.7B) reach 61 tok/s mean but 'silently corrupt JSON & lists' (https://github.com/outsourc-e/qwen36-4090-recipes). Ollama lacks a per-model n-cpu-moe switch (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/11772). Ollama v0.30 integrated llama.cpp as an engine (https://webscraft.org/blog/ollama-030-scho-novogo-gguf-vulkan-llamacpp-i-tool-calling?lang=en).
how_we_use_it: Add an opt-in 'Advanced engine: llama-server' in settings.rs and SettingsPanel. The app downloads a pinned llama.cpp CUDA build for Windows, reuses Ollama's GGUF blobs (path taken from the /api/show modelfile FROM line, so there is no re-download), launches llama-server through winproc.rs with `--fit on --jinja` plus an auto-computed `--n-cpu-moe` for MoE models, and points CodeWhale at it through the existing `[providers.vllm]`/custom OpenAI-compatible route (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1). For Qwen3.6/3.8-27B on 24 GB, offer a 'Speed boost' toggle that adds a Qwen3.5-4B same-vocab draft. Never offer cross-vocab drafts, because tool-call and JSON integrity is non-negotiable for an agent.

name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning / Nemotron 3 Nano (30B-A3B hybrid Mamba-MoE): speed-first agent executor
what: NVIDIA's open 30B-A3B hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE models. Lightning, released August 2026, is tuned for fast agent execution and ships with speculative decoding in its Ollama recipe. Its coding accuracy is clearly below Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, so it suits sub-agent or explore roles rather than the main coder.
date: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning: 2026-08-11; Nemotron 3 Nano: Dec 2025
concrete_claims: Lightning: 30B MoE with about 3B active, OpenMDW-1.1 license, released August 11, 2026; SWE-bench Verified 51.56 (BF16) and 52.80 (NVFP4); Terminal-Bench 2.1 24.58 / 23.46; local recipe `ollama run nemotron-3.5-lightning` with speculative decoding built in (https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4, https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3.5-lightning). Context up to 1M per NGC (https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nim/nvidia/models/nemotron-3.5-lightning/-). Nemotron 3 Nano 30B-A3B: SWE-Bench (OpenHands) 38.8; Ollama `nemotron-3-nano:30b` plus a 4B tag (https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16, https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3-nano). Ollama maps the parser 'nemotron-3-nano'/'nemotron-3.5-nano' (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/model/parsers/parsers.go).
how_we_use_it: Offer it as an optional 'fast helper' model when CodeWhale's sub-agent or explore features are used: the main coder stays on Qwen3.8-27B, and cheap search or summarize steps go to Lightning. Because both models must be resident, the fit estimator must budget both (OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS); on 24 GB this only works with the helper partly offloaded, so show the estimate before enabling it. Run the acceptance test before marking it agent-ready.

name: Legacy and stretch models: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, Qwen3-Coder-Next 80B-A3B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B-A6B, DeepSeek
what: Guidance for models users already have or ask about. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B is still a capable fast non-thinking coder but has been superseded. Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B-A6B) only work on 24 GB GPUs with large system RAM and expert offload. DeepSeek's current open models (V4 Flash/Pro) are far too large, and the old deepseek-r1 distills are poor tool callers.
date: Qwen3-Coder-30B: Jul 2025; Qwen3-Coder-Next: early 2026; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 2026-08-26; DeepSeek V4: 2026-04-24
concrete_claims: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct and Qwen3-Coder-Next have 256K native context; Qwen3-Coder-Next is built on Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Base with hybrid attention, and function calling needs the qwen3_coder tool parser (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder/main/README.md). Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B config: 48 layers, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128, which is 96 KiB of KV per token at f16 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct). Qwen3-Coder-Next tech report: SWE-bench Verified 70.6 (SWE-Agent), 71.1 (MiniSWE-Agent), 71.3 (OpenHands) (https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00729v1); Ollama tag `qwen3-coder-next` (https://dev.to/sienna/qwen3-coder-next-the-complete-2026-guide-to-running-powerful-ai-coding-agents-locally-1k95). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 125B MoE with 6B active, qwen-community-1.0 license, vendor SWE-bench Pro 62.5 (https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/26/alibabas-qwen-team-releases-qwen3-8-flash-next-a-125b-multimodal-moe-with-6b-active-parameters-previewing-the-qwen4-architecture/, https://www.datacamp.com/blog/qwen3-8-flash-next); Ollama lists a 125b-mlx tag (https://ollama.com/library/qwen3.8-flash-next). DeepSeek V4: Pro is 1.6T/49B active and Flash is 284B/13B active, MIT license, 1M context (https://www.morphllm.com/deepseek-v4-flash); Ollama exposes V4-Flash only as a cloud model (https://codersera.com/blog/run-deepseek-v4-flash-locally-full-2026-setup-guide/). `deepseek-r1:8b` has returned 'does not support tools' errors in agent frameworks (https://community.crewai.com/t/llm-used-through-ollama-is-not-working-for-fileread-tool/3611).
how_we_use_it: In the model list (ollama_models in ollama.rs), tag installed legacy models with a 'Superseded' hint and a one-click replacement: deepseek-r1:* and qwen3:4b go to qwen3.5:9b or qwen3.8:27b depending on VRAM, and qwen3-coder:30b goes to qwen3.6:35b-a3b. Mark qwen3-coder-next and qwen3.8-flash-next as 'Stretch: needs at least 64 GB system RAM plus the llama-server expert-offload engine', shown only when free RAM qualifies, with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's non-Apache license noted. For DeepSeek users, explain that V4 runs locally only on server-class hardware and offer CodeWhale's existing DeepSeek or Ollama Cloud provider as the hosted option.

name: Context-window autosizing: Ollama's 4k VRAM-tier default, num_ctx variants and syncing CodeWhale's context_window
what: Ollama now picks a default context from total VRAM: 4k below 24 GiB, 32k for 24–48 GiB, 256k at 48 GiB and up. Its own docs say agents and coding tools need at least 64000 tokens. On a typical 8–16 GB consumer card the default is 4096, so a coding agent silently loses the start of its prompt. The OpenAI-compatible endpoint that CodeWhale uses cannot carry num_ctx.
date: Docs and code as of Ollama main 2026-10-13; latest stable v0.40.3 (2026-10-11)
concrete_claims: VRAM tiers: '< 24 GiB VRAM: 4k context; 24-48 GiB: 32k; >= 48 GiB: 256k'. Docs also say 'Tasks which require large context like web search, agents, and coding tools should be set to at least 64000 tokens' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/context-length.mdx = https://docs.ollama.com/context-length). Code compares against 47/23 GiB thresholds after subtracting OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD, setting defaultNumCtx to 262144/32768/4096 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/server/routes.go). Automatic ctx is used only when neither the request, the Modelfile num_ctx nor OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is set (usesAutomaticNumCtx, same file). When the automatic ctx does not fit, the scheduler steps down 262144→32768→4096 (nextLowerAutoNumCtx in https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/server/sched.go). OpenAI ChatCompletionRequest has no num_ctx field; it does have the Ollama extension keep_alive and reasoning_effort (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/openai/openai.go). /api/ps returns context_length per loaded model (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/api/types.go). Since v0.30.9 Ollama returns an error if a single message is larger than the current context window (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=4). The CodeWhale provider table accepts context_window, and auto-compaction defaults to 80% of the window (auto_compact_threshold_percent) (local cw-src/config.example.toml lines 619, 1357-1361).
how_we_use_it: Turn the existing ollama_create_variant (src-tauri/src/ollama.rs) into a 'Context wizard'. (1) Read GGUF metadata from /api/show (block_count, head_count_kv, key/value_length, context_length) and free VRAM from nvidia-smi, which StatusBar already polls. (2) Compute the largest num_ctx that keeps the model 100% on GPU for the chosen KV type, offering 32k/64k/128k presets with a 'fits fully / will spill' badge. (3) Create '<model>-cw<ctx>k' with parameters {num_ctx}. (4) Write context_window = num_ctx into ~/.codewhale/config.toml [providers.ollama], or into the custom provider table, so CodeWhale compacts at 80% of the real window instead of overflowing. (5) After first load, verify /api/ps context_length and size_vram == size; the Inspector ContextTab mismatch warning already exists, so add a 'Fix' button there. Also offer server-wide OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH as an alternative when a managed server is used (see the managed-server item).

name: KV-cache quantization (q8_0 / q4_0) with llama.cpp's Hadamard attention rotation and auto flash attention
what: Quantizing the K/V cache halves (q8_0) or quarters (q4_0) context memory. Since April 2026, llama.cpp rotates Q/K/V with a Hadamard transform before caching, which makes q8_0 almost lossless and q4_0 usable. Ollama on NVIDIA now runs llama.cpp's llama-server and passes OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE to both caches. Flash attention is automatic.
date: Rotation PR #21038 merged 2026-04-01; Ollama FAQ current as of 2026-10
concrete_claims: OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE: f16 (default), q8_0 (~1/2 memory, 'recommended if not using f16'), q4_0 (~1/4 memory). It is a global option. Flash attention is used automatically when supported, and OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1/0 forces it on or off (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/faq.mdx). Ollama passes '--cache-type-k X --cache-type-v X' and '--flash-attn auto' to llama-server (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/llama_server.go). PR #21038 'rotate activations for better quantization' was merged 2026-04-01. Qwen3.5-9B mean KLD: f16/f16 0.000782, q8_0/q8_0 0.000799, q4_0/q4_0 0.004782. gpt-oss-20b AIME25: Q4_0 KV 2.0%→21.7% and Q8_0 31.7%→37.1% vs F16 37.9%. Token generation is about 0.88–0.93x on Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_0 CUDA (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/21038). Opt-out env LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/llama-kv-cache.cpp). Allowed llama-server cache types: f32, f16, bf16, q8_0, q4_0, q4_1, iq4_nl, q5_0, q5_1 (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md). v0.31.2 enabled flash attention on NVIDIA compute capability 6.x (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=4). Caveat: issue #25382 (2026-07-07) reported garbage output on DeepSeek-V4 with a q8_0 K-cache because of rotation; the workaround is an f16 K-cache. It was closed the same day (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25382).
how_we_use_it: Add a 'KV cache' segmented control in SettingsPanel → Ollama: f16 / q8_0 (default recommendation) / q4_0 ('max context'). Changing it rewrites the managed-server environment and restarts Ollama; this is required because the setting is server-global. The Context wizard then recomputes the maximum num_ctx (about 2x more tokens at q8_0). Leave OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION unset (auto). Show a per-model warning to fall back to f16 for DeepSeek-family models if output degrades, since the user previously ran deepseek locally. For the llama.cpp provider, expose K and V separately (e.g. -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0) in the generated preset.

name: llama.cpp --fit auto-placement with automatic MoE expert offload to CPU (inside Ollama ≥0.30)
what: Ollama 0.30 (May 2026) switched its GGUF engine on NVIDIA to upstream llama-server. It passes almost no placement flags, so llama.cpp's --fit (on by default) decides layer placement. When VRAM is short, fit first keeps dense or attention weights on GPU and moves sparse MoE expert tensors to system RAM. That makes 35B-A3B-class MoE models usable on 6–16 GB cards.
date: Ollama v0.30.0 May 2026; fit/MoE logic in llama.cpp master 2026-10-13
concrete_claims: Ollama v0.30.0 'adds llama.cpp for improved compatibility and performance … faster performance on NVIDIA hardware' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=5). Ollama builds a 'minimal set, let llama-server auto-detect the rest' and passes -ngl only when num_gpu is set explicitly (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/llama_server.go). Ollama documents server env LLAMA_ARG_FIT ('default "on"') and LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET ('Target free VRAM margin per device … (MiB)') (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/envconfig/config.go). llama-server: '-fit, --fit [on|off]' default on; '-fitt, --fit-target' default 1024 MiB; '-fitc, --fit-ctx' minimum 4096; '-ncmoe, --n-cpu-moe N'; '-cmoe, --cpu-moe' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md). fit step 3: 'for a MoE model, same as dense model but with all MoE tensors in system memory' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/common/fit.cpp). The llama-fit-params tool prints the fitted CLI args without loading (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/fit-params/README.md). Community (2026-03-29), RTX 2060 6 GB laptop on Windows 11, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q4_K_M with --n-cpu-moe 99, -ctk/-ctv q8_0, -c 102144: about 15 tok/s generation and 350–400 tok/s prefill (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/21112). Caveat: fit aborts if the user already set tensor_buft_overrides (common/fit.cpp).
how_we_use_it: (1) Require Ollama ≥0.30 (recommend ≥0.40.3) in useBootstrap and show a banner on older versions. (2) Never send num_gpu by default, because that disables fit. (3) Add a 'Reserve VRAM for other apps (Godot editor, browser)' slider that maps to LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET in MiB on the managed server; default 1024, suggest 2048 when Godot is running. (4) In the model picker, mark MoE models (expert_count > 0 in /api/show model_info) as 'good for small GPU: experts go to RAM'. Show the measured split from /api/ps (size_vram vs size), which Inspector already shows, and add a short note explaining that partial offload of a MoE model is expected and fine. (5) For the llama.cpp provider, run llama-fit-params --model X -c N before launch and show the fitted -ngl/-ot result as a 'Fit preview'. Do not inject LLAMA_ARG_N_CPU_MOE into Ollama: it conflicts with fit.

name: MTP speculative decoding (model's own multi-token-prediction heads) via Ollama draft_num_predict / llama.cpp --spec-type draft-mtp
what: Some models (Qwen3.5/3.6, Gemma 4, GLM, DeepSeek and others) ship MTP heads that draft several tokens, which the main model then verifies losslessly. llama.cpp merged MTP in May 2026. Ollama's llama-server path enables it only when draft_num_predict is set. The default for embedded MTP is 0 (off).
date: llama.cpp PR #22673 merged ~2026-05-16; Ollama draft_num_predict in docs as of 2026-10
concrete_claims: PR #22673 'llama + spec: MTP Support' was merged around 2026-05-16 and uses '--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max N'. Reported results: RTX 3090+3060, 27B Q6_K, 22.97→42.45 tok/s (~1.85x) at n-max 3 with 76% acceptance. Prefill dropped 1315→665 tok/s, and MTP added ~2.49 GiB VRAM. RTX 5090 27B: 63.72→105.47 tok/s. 6 GB laptop, 35B-A3B: 22.92→29.39 tok/s at n-max 2 (81.5% acceptance). The early version required n_parallel=1 (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22673). Ollama Modelfile: 'draft_num_predict … Separate draft models default to 4; embedded MTP tensors require setting this parameter. Set to 0 to disable' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/modelfile.mdx). Ollama zeroes DraftNumPredict when the model has no separate draft and the parameter is unset (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/server/routes.go). It detects MTP by nextn_predict_layers > 0 or qwen35 'mtp.' tensors, and passes '--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max N --spec-draft-backend-sampling' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/llama_server.go). On Apple MLX, Ollama made MTP automatic: v0.31.1 Gemma 4 'nearly 90% faster' on a coding-agent benchmark; v0.32.6 Qwen3.5 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=4, https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=3). llama.cpp archs with nextn layers include qwen35moe, qwen3next, glm4, deepseek2/4, nemotron-h and gemma4-assistant (src/models in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp).
how_we_use_it: In ollama_models (src-tauri/src/ollama.rs), add an 'mtp' capability flag when /api/show model_info contains a '*.nextn_predict_layers' key > 0. Verify the key name on the target build. In the variant dialog, add a 'Speed boost (MTP)' toggle that passes parameters {num_ctx, draft_num_predict: 2} to /api/create (2 is the best value in the 6 GB report; 3 for larger GPUs). Add a one-click A/B bench: send the same 300-token coding prompt to the base model and the MTP variant, then read 'timings.predicted_per_second' and prompt_per_second from the OpenAI response. Keep the variant only if generation improves and prefill loss is acceptable, because agent turns are often prefill-heavy. Budget ~10% extra VRAM in the Context wizard.

name: Prompt/KV prefix-cache hygiene for agent loops (cached_tokens, checkpoints for hybrid models, keep_alive)
what: In agent loops most of each request repeats the previous prompt, so local speed depends on reusing the KV prefix. Ollama now reports cached prompt tokens and fixed several agent-specific cache breakers. Hybrid/recurrent models (Qwen3.5/3.6 family) can only roll back to saved checkpoints. Unloading the model (default keep_alive 5m) throws the whole cache away.
concrete_claims: v0.30.8: 'Improved prompt caching by decoupling it from context shift for better KV cache reuse'. v0.33.0 fixed a hang when agent clients cancel long prefills. It also fixed a restore-point bug that 'had forced a 46k-of-47k-token request to reprocess from zero on models with recurrent layers', and removed a Claude Code 'tokens left' message that broke the KV cache on every request. v0.33.3: 'Report cached prompt tokens'. v0.32.15: TTFT ~995 ms→~524 ms from metadata caching (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=2, https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=4). OpenAI responses include usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and a llama.cpp-style 'timings' object (prompt_per_second, predicted_per_second) (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/openai/openai.go). OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE default '5m'; negative values keep the model loaded forever (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/faq.mdx). llama-server: '--cache-ram' default 8192 MiB host prompt cache; '--ctx-checkpoints' default 32 per slot; '--checkpoint-min-step' default 8192 tokens; '--cache-reuse N'; response timings.cache_n = prompt tokens reused (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md).
how_we_use_it: (1) If app-server events carry usage, add a StatusBar segment 'Cache 92% · 41 tok/s' per turn, computed from cached_tokens/prompt_tokens and timings. Alert when the hit rate collapses on a long thread, which means a prefix breaker such as a timestamp or reordered system prompt. (2) Default the managed server to OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=2h (or -1 with an 'Unload' button; ollama_unload already exists), so stepping away for 6 minutes does not cost a full re-prefill of a 50k-token context. (3) For Qwen3.5/3.6-family models, prefer CodeWhale settings that only append to history; trigger compaction rarely (the threshold item), since every rewrite of earlier context forces re-prefill from the last checkpoint. (4) Before a long session, warm up the model with POST /api/generate {model, keep_alive}.

name: Managed Ollama server with env profiles (Windows): one-click apply of server-global settings
what: Context length, KV type, keep-alive, parallelism, VRAM margin and model path are server-global environment variables read at startup. The Windows tray app only picks them up after a quit and relaunch. Ollama ships a standalone ollama-windows-amd64.zip meant for embedding 'ollama serve' in other apps, so the desktop can own the server process and its configuration.
date: Ollama main 2026-10-13 (v0.40.3 latest stable 2026-10-11)
concrete_claims: envconfig vars: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH ('default: 4k/32k/256k based on VRAM'), OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE, OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION, OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE (5m), OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL (1), OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS, OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE (512), OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD ('Reserve a portion of VRAM per GPU (bytes)'), OLLAMA_LOAD_TIMEOUT (5m), OLLAMA_MODELS, OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD, OLLAMA_VULKAN, LLAMA_ARG_FIT, LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/envconfig/config.go). Windows docs: after setting env vars, 'Quit the tray application and relaunch it'. A 'standalone ollama-windows-amd64.zip … allows for embedding Ollama in existing applications, or running it as a system service via ollama serve with tools such as NSSM'. Logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama (server.log) (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/windows.mdx). The llama-server child inherits the Ollama process environment (cmd.Env = os.Environ() in https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/llama_server.go). v0.40.2 background-upgrades older models, and 'downgrading below 0.40 requires re-pulling the models' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases).
how_we_use_it: Add an 'Ollama mode' setting in src-tauri/src/settings.rs: 'external' (current behaviour, read-only, ollamaUrl) or 'managed'. In managed mode, Tauri starts a bundled or user-located ollama.exe serve on 127.0.0.1:11434, or a private port to avoid clashing with the tray app. It passes an env profile built from the UI (ctx, KV type, keep_alive, NUM_PARALLEL, LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET, OLLAMA_MODELS on a fast NVMe) and restarts on change. It tails server.log into a 'Server log' panel and parses 'llama_params_fit' overflow lines to explain spills. Ship three presets: 'Max quality' (f16 KV, 32k), 'Agent' (q8_0 KV, 64k, keep_alive 2h) and 'Small GPU' (q4_0 KV, 32k, MoE-first model suggestions). Warn before upgrades because of the 0.40 migration.

name: llama.cpp llama-server as a first-class managed provider (router mode + INI presets)
what: Upstream llama-server exposes everything Ollama hides: per-model presets, split K/V types, n-gram and model-based speculative decoding, manual MoE offload, reasoning budgets, idle sleep, and a router that loads models on demand. It installs on Windows via winget, and CodeWhale can reach it as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider.
concrete_claims: Router mode: launch llama-server without a model. It uses '--models-dir PATH', '--models-preset PATH' (INI), and '--models-max N' (default 4); the request's 'model' field routes it. Preset keys mirror CLI args, e.g. 'n-gpu-layers = 123', 'model-draft = …', 'LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM = 0', plus preset-only 'load-on-startup' and 'stop-timeout' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md, https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/preset.md). '--sleep-idle-seconds' (PR #18228). '-np, --parallel N' default -1 = auto. '--kv-unified-per-slot N'. '--reasoning-budget N', '--reasoning-effort LEVEL'. '-bs, --backend-sampling' (experimental). '--metrics' (README). Install: 'winget install llama.cpp'; conda-forge has CUDA and Vulkan builds for Windows (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md). Latest build tag b11599 and release v0.6.0, 05 Oct (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/v0.6.0). CodeWhale custom provider: [providers.<name>] kind = "openai-compatible", base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1" (local cw-src/docs/CONFIGURATION.md ~L588-598).
how_we_use_it: Add an 'Engine: Ollama | llama.cpp' switch. In llama.cpp mode, the desktop detects llama-server.exe (winget path or a user-picked folder) and generates %APPDATA%/CodeWhale/llamacpp-presets.ini from the same UI controls (ctx, -ctk/-ctv, spec-type, n-cpu-moe, reasoning-budget, sleep-idle-seconds 900). It launches 'llama-server --models-dir <GGUF dir> --models-preset <ini> --models-max 1 --port 8081 --no-webui' and writes [providers.llamacpp] kind="openai-compatible", base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1", context_window=<ctx> into the CodeWhale config. This is the 'power-user' path for users with GGUFs from Hugging Face (Unsloth MTP/MXFP4 quants) and for Godot shader loops that benefit from n-gram drafting.

name: Draftless n-gram speculative decoding (ngram-mod / ngram-simple) for code rewriting
what: llama.cpp can draft tokens from n-grams already present in the context, with no extra model and about 16 MB of memory. This is very effective when the model re-emits existing code: whole-file edits, apply_patch context, and fixing a shader after a compile error. Ollama does not expose it; only llama-server does.
date: ngram-mod PR #19164 merged 2026-01-30; docs current 2026-10
concrete_claims: Spec types include ngram-cache, ngram-simple, ngram-map-k, ngram-map-k4v and ngram-mod. ngram-mod is 'Lightweight (~16 MB)' with 'Constant memory and complexity', and one hash pool is shared across slots. Listed applications: 'Iterating over a block of text/code', reasoning models repeating their thinking, summarization. 'If a draft model is combined with a draftless decoding the draftless decoding has higher precedence' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/speculative.md). '--spec-default' enables ngram-mod with n_match 24, n_min 48, n_max 64 (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/common/arg.cpp). PR #19164 user reports: gpt-oss-120b verbatim repeat at 0.92 acceptance, ~814 tok/s. One CRLF file went from 2.32 tok/s (11/96 accepted) to 29.79 tok/s (518/624) when switched to LF (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/19164). Ollama only passes --spec-type for draft-mtp/draft-dflash/external drafts (appendDraftArgs in https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/llama_server.go).
how_we_use_it: In the llama.cpp provider presets, add 'spec-default = 1' by default for coding models (or spec-type = ngram-mod), with a 'Code-rewrite turbo' toggle. Show the acceptance rate from llama-server timings and logs in the Inspector. For the Godot shader skill and compile-check loop, keep the shader source in context verbatim, because n-gram drafting then accelerates the corrected re-emit. Because of the CRLF report, suggest normalising .gdshader/.gd files to LF (or warn when the workspace uses CRLF). A Windows-specific tip.

name: Parallel slots vs CodeWhale sub-agents (OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL, forced single slot for hybrid models)
what: CodeWhale can fan out many sub-agents, but a local server serves one request at a time by default. Each parallel slot multiplies KV memory. Ollama silently forces one slot for several hybrid or recurrent architectures, including the Qwen3.5/3.6 family.
date: Ollama main 2026-10-13; LM Studio 0.4.x docs 2026-10
concrete_claims: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL default 1. 'Required RAM will scale by OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL * OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH'. OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE default 512 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/faq.mdx). Ollama launches llama-server with '-c NumCtx*numParallel -np numParallel' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/llama_server.go). The scheduler sets numParallel = 1 for families mllama, qwen3vl, qwen3vlmoe, qwen35, qwen35moe, qwen3next, lfm2, lfm2moe, nemotron_h, nemotron_h_moe and nemotron_h_omni ('model architecture does not currently support parallel requests') (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/server/sched.go). CodeWhale: 'max_subagents = 64 # optional (default 64, clamped to 1-128)'; '[subagents] max_concurrent' overrides it (https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale, config.example.toml L319, L516-519). LM Studio: 'Max Concurrent Predictions' defaults to 4 via llama.cpp continuous batching and needs the llama.cpp runtime v2.0.0 (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/blob/main/0_app/5_advanced/parallel-requests.md). llama-server '-np' auto and '--kv-unified-per-slot N' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md).
how_we_use_it: Add a 'Parallel requests' control (1/2/4). It sets OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL on the managed server and also writes [subagents] max_concurrent = same value into the CodeWhale config, so sub-agents do not pile up in Ollama's queue and hit api_timeout_secs. The Context wizard divides available KV memory by the slot count. If the selected model's family is in Ollama's forced-1 list (from /api/show details.family), lock the control at 1 with an explanation, and suggest the llama.cpp provider when parallel sub-agents matter.

name: Windows GPU hygiene: NVIDIA Sysmem Fallback policy, VRAM reserve for Godot, Vulkan/driver checks
what: On Windows, the NVIDIA driver can silently spill CUDA allocations into shared system memory instead of failing. Tokens/s then collapses without an error. The desktop compositor and the Godot editor also take VRAM from the same GPU. A desktop app can detect and fix these issues.
date: NVIDIA setting since driver 546.01 (2023); Ollama Windows notes 2026
concrete_claims: NVIDIA added a setting to disable the shared-memory fallback in driver 546.01 and above: NVIDIA Control Panel → 'CUDA - Sysmem Fallback Policy' → 'Prefer No Sysmem Fallback'. Trade-off: stable performance 'at the risk of a crash' if more memory is needed (https://nvidia.custhelp.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/5490, https://borncity.com/blog/2023/11/26/windows-10-11-hardware-beschleunigte-gpu-planung-und-nvidia-cuda-policy/). Ollama Windows requirements: NVIDIA driver 551.61+. Vulkan is enabled by default as the AMD fallback. GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES selects the dGPU on hybrid systems. Logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\server.log (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/windows.mdx). OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD reserves VRAM per GPU in bytes (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/envconfig/config.go). v0.30.11 fixed 'ollama ps double-counting mmap'd weights on partial offload', fixed inverted iGPU/dGPU Vulkan classification on Windows, and added sm_86 to the cuda_v13_windows preset (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=4).
how_we_use_it: Add a 'GPU health' check to StatusScreens/Settings. (1) Read the driver version with nvidia-smi and warn below 551.61. (2) Detect a spill: Windows 'Shared GPU memory' rises while nvidia-smi dedicated usage is at its cap and tok/s drops; then show a guided card for 'Prefer No Sysmem Fallback', which needs a manual Control Panel step and an app restart. (3) If godot*.exe is running, automatically raise LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET / OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD by the editor's measured VRAM (nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps) before loading the model. (4) Offer OLLAMA_MODELS relocation to the fastest NVMe to cut load time.

name: Quantization formats in 2026: Q4_K_M / IQ4_XS, QAT tags, MXFP4, and native NVFP4 on RTX 50 (Blackwell)
what: Weight-format choice sets both what fits on the GPU and how fast it runs. Quantization-aware-trained (QAT) tags retain quality at 4 bits. MXFP4 is gpt-oss's native format and the MXFP4_MOE recipe. NVFP4 and MXFP4 use Blackwell FP4 tensor cores in llama.cpp CUDA, so RTX 50 owners get faster prefill.
date: Ollama Gemma 4 QAT v0.30.6 (Jun 2026); llama.cpp NVFP4 Mar–Apr 2026
concrete_claims: ggml types: GGML_TYPE_MXFP4 = 39 'MXFP4 (1 block)' and GGML_TYPE_NVFP4 = 40 'NVFP4 (4 blocks, E4M3 scale)' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/include/ggml.h). The quantize tool has the 'MXFP4_MOE' recipe (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/quantize/quantize.cpp). The CUDA backend defines BLACKWELL_MMA_AVAILABLE for sm_120 'used for NVFP4' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh). Ollama v0.30.6 added Gemma 4 QAT tags 'gemma4:e2b-it-qat' through 'gemma4:31b-it-qat'. v0.34.1: 'GGUF model creation now requires using llama.cpp tooling for safetensor conversion and quantization' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=5, https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=2). NVIDIA (CES 2026) claimed 35% (llama.cpp) and 30% (Ollama) SLM inference gains over four months, from GPU token sampling and CUDA-graph/kernel work (https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/open-source-ai-tool-upgrades-speed-up-llm-and-diffusion-models-on-nvidia-rtx-pcs). Secondary report: an RTX 5090 running Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 went from 3,295 to 5,547 tok/s prefill (pp512), with decode flat at ~73.6 tok/s (https://insiderllm.com/guides/fp4-inference-llamacpp-nvfp4-mxfp4/).
how_we_use_it: In the model picker, show details.quantization_level from /api/tags and /api/show next to size and estimated KV. Add a 'Recommended for your GPU' hint: on compute capability 12.x (RTX 50, read via nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap) prefer NVFP4/MXFP4 builds; on others prefer -qat tags, then Q4_K_M, then IQ4_XS when VRAM is tight. Weight prefill speed heavily, because agent turns are prefill-bound. Never auto-pull. Present the choice and the size delta.

name: Reasoning/thinking budget control for local models
what: On a single consumer GPU, thinking tokens dominate wall-clock time per agent step. Ollama now reports per-model thinking controls and accepts reasoning_effort over its OpenAI-compatible API. llama-server can cap thinking with a hard token budget.
date: Ollama v0.34.3 (Sep 2026); llama.cpp README 2026-10
concrete_claims: Ollama v0.34.3: 'GET /api/show now reports each model's thinking controls and default' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases). OpenAI ChatCompletionRequest accepts 'reasoning' {effort} and 'reasoning_effort' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/openai/openai.go). llama-server: '--reasoning-budget N' (-1 unrestricted, 0 immediate end), '--reasoning-budget-message', and '--reasoning-effort LEVEL' ('minimal','low','medium','high','xhigh','max') (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md). v0.32.10: models without a repeat_penalty now default to 1.0 'instead of 1.1', which the notes say speeds up speculative decoding (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=3).
how_we_use_it: Read the thinking controls from /api/show in ollama_models and render a per-model 'Thinking: off/low/high' pill in the Toolbar, mapped to CodeWhale's reasoning preference, which already exists in crates/tui/src/reasoning_preference.rs. Default 'low' for edit/apply steps and 'high' for planning. For the llama.cpp provider, write reasoning-budget = 2048 into the preset as a guardrail against runaway thinking on small models such as qwen3-4b.

name: LM Studio 0.4.x as an alternative provider (llmster headless daemon, REST load with per-model context)
what: LM Studio 0.4 added llmster, a GUI-less daemon installable on Windows. It also added parallel requests via continuous batching, a native REST API that loads models with an explicit context length, flash-attention flag and KV-offload setting, and OpenAI Responses plus Anthropic Messages compatibility on port 1234.
date: LM Studio 0.4.0/0.4.1 (2026); docs repo HEAD 2026-10-08
concrete_claims: llmster install on Windows: 'irm https://lmstudio.ai/install.ps1 | iex'; start with 'lms daemon up' (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/blob/main/1_developer/0_core/headless.md). 'POST /api/v1/models/load' takes context_length, eval_batch_size, flash_attention, num_experts, offload_kv_cache_to_gpu and echo_load_config (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/blob/main/1_developer/2_rest/load.md). 'lms load' flags: --ttl, --gpu (0-1|off|max), --context-length, --identifier, --estimate-only (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/blob/main/3_cli/0_local-models/load.md). The API changelog lists 0.4.1 'POST /v1/messages' (Anthropic-compatible), 0.4.0 native REST /api/v1/*, and 0.3.29 (2025-10-06) 'POST /v1/responses' (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/blob/main/1_developer/api-changelog.md). Max Concurrent Predictions defaults to 4 (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/blob/main/0_app/5_advanced/parallel-requests.md).
how_we_use_it: Auto-detect http://127.0.0.1:1234 at startup in useBootstrap. Offer 'Use LM Studio' to write the custom provider [providers.lm-studio] kind="openai-compatible", which CodeWhale already supports and tests. Before a session, call POST /api/v1/models/load {model, context_length, flash_attention: true, echo_load_config: true}, so the context is set without the Modelfile-variant workaround. Read back load_config and sync context_window. Use 'lms load --estimate-only' for a pre-load memory estimate in the Context wizard.

name: Trained draft models: DFlash, DSpark, EAGLE-3 (paired with a specific target)
what: Newer speculative-decoding drafters read the target model's hidden states. DFlash drafts a whole block in one forward pass (block diffusion); DSpark adds a Markov head. Both reach much higher acceptance than a standalone small model. llama.cpp supports all three. Ollama on NVIDIA accepts DFlash and external drafts in models it packages.
date: DFlash arXiv 2602.06036 (Feb 2026); llama.cpp docs 2026-10; Ollama DFlash v0.32.7-0.32.8 (Aug 2026)
concrete_claims: DFlash (arXiv 2602.06036): authors report over 6x lossless acceleration and up to 2.5x the speedup of EAGLE-3. Their benchmarks ran on B200 GPUs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06036). llama.cpp: '--spec-type draft-dflash' example 'llama-server -m Qwen3-4B.gguf -md Qwen3-4B-DFlash.gguf --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 15 -fa on --jinja'. DSpark example 'deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7' with '--spec-draft-n-max 7' ('only drafts with a Qwen3 backbone are supported'). The EAGLE-3 list includes AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3, RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-speculator.eagle3 and RedHatAI/gpt-oss-20b-speculator.eagle3 (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/speculative.md). Ollama defines draftTypeDFlash = "draft-dflash" and detects external draft types (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/llama_server.go). v0.32.8 Muse Glimmer 'support for DFlash'; v0.32.4 'Quantize draft-model output heads … when creating speculative-decoding drafts' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases?page=3).
how_we_use_it: In the llama.cpp provider, keep a small curated 'target → draft' table: Qwen3-4B → z-lab DFlash or DSpark (the user already runs qwen3-4b-32k), and gemma-4-26B-A4B → EAGLE-3. Offer one click to download the draft GGUF and add 'model-draft' plus 'spec-type' lines to the preset. Show measured acceptance and tok/s versus no-draft using the same A/B bench as the MTP item. Mark it experimental, because drafts are target-specific and the paper's 6x figure is from datacenter GPUs.

name: vLLM / SGLang (WSL2 only) and ExLlamaV3 + TabbyAPI (native Windows): advanced backends to detect, not bundle
what: vLLM and SGLang give the best batched throughput but are Linux-first; on Windows they run under WSL2 or Docker. ExLlamaV3 (EXL3, QTIP-based quantization, 2–8-bit cache, MTP and n-gram drafting) runs on native Windows through TabbyAPI. TabbyAPI describes itself as a hobby project.
date: vLLM v0.31.0 tag, docs 2026-10-13; ExLlamaV3 v1.6.1, README 2026-10-11; TabbyAPI 2026-10-13
concrete_claims: vLLM docs: 'vLLM does not support Windows natively. To run vLLM on Windows, you can use the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) … or use some community-maintained forks, e.g. https://github.com/SystemPanic/vllm-windows' (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.md). Docker Model Runner added vLLM on Windows through WSL2 (Docker Desktop 4.54+, NVIDIA compute capability ≥8.0) (https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-model-runner-vllm-windows/). An SGLang docs snippet advises 'on Windows run under WSL2, and keep the checkpoint inside the ext4 side … never on /mnt/c' (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang, docs/src/snippets/configs/MiniMaxAI/minimax-h3.jsx). ExLlamaV3: 'EXL3, based on QTIP, plus 2–8 bit cache quantization', CPU offloading for large MoE, speculative decoding. On Windows it needs the 'triton-windows' package (https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/blob/master/README.md). TabbyAPI: OpenAI-compatible on port 5000; cache_mode 'k_bits,v_bits … 2-8'; draft_mode 'model, disabled, mtp, ngram'; 'a hobby project … not meant to run on production servers' (https://github.com/theroyallab/tabbyAPI/blob/main/README.md, https://github.com/theroyallab/tabbyAPI/blob/main/config_sample.yml). CodeWhale already has provider kinds sglang and vllm (base_url http://localhost:30000/v1 and http://localhost:8000/v1) (https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale, config.example.toml).
how_we_use_it: Add an 'Advanced backends' section that only probes known ports: 8000 for vLLM (WSL2 forwards localhost), 30000 for SGLang and 5000 for TabbyAPI. When a probe answers, offer to write the matching CodeWhale provider (vllm, sglang, or a custom openai-compatible provider for TabbyAPI) with context_window read from /v1/models. Do not install or manage these backends. Recommend them only for users who need many parallel sub-agents (vLLM/SGLang) or the best quality per VRAM with EXL3 on a 16–24 GB card (TabbyAPI).

name: Context-window autopilot for Ollama: auto-fit and pin num_ctx, detect silent truncation
what: Ollama picks a default context window based on VRAM, and it is 4k below 24 GiB. Its OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint (the one CodeWhale uses) cannot set num_ctx. Overflow has historically been dropped silently. Auto-fitting the largest num_ctx that keeps the model 100% on GPU, and pinning it per model, is the most important reliability fix for a local agent.
concrete_claims:
- Ollama docs give these defaults: '< 24 GiB VRAM: 4k context, 24-48 GiB: 32k, >= 48 GiB: 256k'. They also say agents and coding tools 'should be set to at least 64000 tokens', and to check the CPU/GPU split and CONTEXT with `ollama ps` (https://docs.ollama.com/context-length, source https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/context-length.mdx). The tiers shipped in 0.15.5 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/14073). That issue also reports the 256k default spilling to CPU on a 52 GB machine.
- The OpenAI-compat doc says: 'The OpenAI API does not have a way of setting the context size for a model'. The fix it gives is a Modelfile with `PARAMETER num_ctx` plus `ollama create` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api/openai-compatibility.mdx).
- Aider quantization study (2024-11-21) on Qwen2.5-Coder-32B fp16 in Ollama: 71.4% pass with 90.2% well-formed edits at >=8k ctx, versus 51.9% pass with 46.2% well-formed at Ollama's then-default 2k. It says Ollama 'silently truncates the request by discarding the oldest messages' (https://aider.chat/2024/11/21/quantization.html, data https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/website/_data/quant.yml).
- Changing num_ctx between requests forces a full model reload, because the KV cache is allocated at load time. One secondary report measured about 140 s per reload for a 17 GB model (https://dev.to/pat9000/pin-your-context-window-or-pay-the-reload-tax-3nfo).
- /api/ps returns `context_length` and `size_vram` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/api/types.go). llm/server.go clamps num_ctx to the training context and warns 'requested context size too large for model' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/server.go).
- Ollama FAQ on memory: OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE defaults to f16. q8_0 uses about 1/2 the memory with 'very small loss in precision', and q4_0 about 1/4. Flash attention turns on automatically when supported (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/faq.mdx). The llama.cpp docs warn that 'extreme KV quantizations (e.g. -ctk q4_0) ... can substantially degrade the model's tool calling performance' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/function-calling.md).
how_we_use_it:
Build on what Desktop already has: `ollama_create_variant` and `ollama_models` (num_ctx/native_ctx) in src-tauri/src/ollama.rs, and `gpu_stats` via nvidia-smi in src-tauri/src/system.rs.
(1) Add a 'Fit context' step that runs automatically on model select. Read /api/show model_info (block_count, head_count_kv, key/value length) and compute KV bytes per token for f16 vs q8_0. Subtract the weight size plus about 1 GB of headroom from free VRAM. Pick the largest num_ctx that fits, capped at native_ctx.
(2) Create a `<model>-cw<N>k` variant with POST /api/create {from, parameters:{num_ctx}}. Warm-load it, then check /api/ps: size_vram==size (100% GPU) and context_length==requested. If either fails, step down.
(3) Write the real window into CodeWhale's route config. Then crates/runtime/src/context_budget.rs computes its ~75% compaction trigger from the true window, not the model's advertised 128k.
(4) Add a truncation guard. Compare Ollama's reported prompt tokens (usage.prompt_tokens / prompt_eval_count) with CodeWhale's own estimate. If the reported count is clearly lower, or pinned at num_ctx, show a red 'history was cut' banner and force compaction.
(5) Add an Ollama settings page that recommends OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0, never q4_0 for agent work, and states that num_ctx is never varied per request.
date: Ollama context-length docs current as of Oct 2026 (VRAM tiers since v0.15.5); Aider study 2024-11-21

name: Deterministic verify-on-edit loop (compile/lint feedback attached to every edit result)
what: Run a project-specific checker automatically after every file mutation and put the result in the edit tool's own output. A small model then gets compiler feedback without having to remember to ask for it. This generalizes the existing Godot shader compile-check into a native feature (the SWE-agent 'linter guardrail' / Agentless 'patch validation' idea).
concrete_claims:
- SWE-agent ACI docs: 'We add a linter that runs when an edit command is issued, and do not let the edit command go through if the code isn't syntactically correct' (https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/blob/main/docs/background/aci.md; paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793, 2024).
- Agentless (arXiv 2407.01489, Jul 2024) has three phases: localization, repair, and patch validation with regression and generated reproduction tests. It reported 32.00% (96 fixes) on SWE-bench Lite at $0.70 per issue (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01489).
- Godot CLI: `--check-only` means 'Only parse for errors and quit (use with --script)' (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.1/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html). A secondary guide warns that the exit code can be 0 on errors, so parse stderr (https://skills.sh/sethcarney/custom-plugins/godot-cli).
- CodeWhale today (local source): crates/tui/src/tools/syntax_check.rs gates edits with syn/toml_edit/serde_json only. crates/tui/src/tools/verifier.rs `run_verifiers` supports up to 12 custom gates (MAX_CUSTOM_GATES=12, default timeout 180000 ms).
- Tree-sitter grammars exist for Godot: tree-sitter-gdscript crate v6.1.0, MIT (https://github.com/PrestonKnopp/tree-sitter-gdscript), and tree-sitter-gdshader (https://github.com/GodOfAvacyn/tree-sitter-gdshader).
how_we_use_it:
Add a per-workspace verifier map, set in Desktop settings or a `.codewhale/verify.toml`, that maps globs to commands:
- `**/*.gdshader` → `powershell -NoProfile -File tools\check-shader.ps1 {path}` (the user's existing script that prints COMPILES / SHADER ERRORS)
- `**/*.gd` → `godot --headless --check-only --script {path}` (judge by stderr)
- `*.rs` → `cargo check --message-format short`
After every successful write_file/edit/apply_patch, CodeWhale runs the matching gate through the existing verifier.rs custom-gate path and appends a compact verdict (at most 12 error lines with line:col) to that tool result. The rule no longer depends on a 4B model obeying AGENTS.md. Cap auto-fix attempts at 3 per file, then escalate: raise the think level (thinking-budget item) or ask the user. Extend syntax_check.rs with tree-sitter parsing (GDScript, gdshader, TS, Python) so newly introduced syntax errors are rejected before the write. Desktop: show a green/red 'COMPILES' badge on each edited file in the diff card, with errors clickable to open at line:col.
date: SWE-agent May 2024; Agentless Jul 2024; Godot 4.x CLI docs

name: Tool-call robustness ladder: model-specific parsers, name/arg repair, schema-constrained re-ask, text-action fallback
what: Small local models often emit tool calls in the wrong dialect: XML instead of JSON, calls inside the text, wrong-case names, truncated args. A layered repair ladder recovers most of these cheaply. Ending it with a grammar-constrained regeneration of only the arguments turns 'model broke the loop' into a single extra call.
concrete_claims:
- Ollama has per-model output parsers selected by name, including 'qwen3', 'qwen3-thinking', 'qwen3-coder', 'harmony', 'deepseek3', 'gemma4', 'ministral' and more (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/model/parsers/parsers.go). Qwen3-Coder emits XML-style calls: `<tool_call><function=NAME><parameter=K>v</parameter></function></tool_call>` (vLLM qwen3coder parser, https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.10.2/api/vllm/entrypoints/openai/tool_parsers/qwen3coder_tool_parser.html).
- Ollama /v1 does NOT support `tool_choice` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api/openai-compatibility.mdx). Streaming with tool calls has been supported since 2025-05-28 (https://ollama.com/blog/streaming-tool).
- llama.cpp has native tool-call handlers for Llama 3.x, Functionary, Hermes 2/3 / Qwen 2.5, Mistral Nemo, Firefunction v2, Command R7B, DeepSeek R1 and GPT-OSS. Other templates fall back to 'Chat format: Generic'. `"parallel_tool_calls": true` is off by default. Lazy grammars came in PR #9639, with trigger patterns in PR #12034 (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/function-calling.md).
- Vercel AI SDK `repairToolCall` docs: 'Language models sometimes fail to generate valid tool calls, especially when the input schema is complex or the model is smaller'.
