The strategies it lists are regenerating inputs with structured outputs, asking a stronger model, or re-asking (https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/content/docs/03-ai-sdk-core/15-tools-and-tool-calling.mdx).
- Ollama `format` accepts a JSON schema, and the docs say 'It is ideal to also pass the JSON schema as a string in the prompt' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/capabilities/structured-outputs.mdx).
- mini-SWE-agent has only bash and 'doesn't even need to use the tool-calling interface of the LMs'. It scores >74% on SWE-bench Verified with frontier models (https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent).
how_we_use_it:
CodeWhale already has crates/tui/src/tools/arg_repair.rs (a 5-stage JSON ladder that flags structure_synthesized) and crates/core/src/tool_parser.rs (text fallback for [TOOL_CALL], <codewhale:tool_call>, <tool_call, <invoke). Extend it in four ways:
(a) Add parsers for the Qwen3-Coder `<function=..><parameter=..>` XML, Mistral `[TOOL_CALLS]`, and fenced ```json {name, arguments}``` blocks.
(b) Repair tool names: case-fold, strip '_tool', and fuzzy-match against the registry. file.rs already aliases argument names.
(c) Schema-constrained re-ask. When args fail schema validation or arg_repair synthesized structure, make one hidden non-streamed native POST /api/chat with `format` = that tool's input schema, think=false, and the last few messages plus 'Re-emit only the arguments for <tool>'. Splice the result in without polluting history.
(d) Capability gate. If /api/show capabilities lacks 'tools', switch the session to a text-action protocol (one fenced action block per turn, mini-SWE-agent style) parsed by tool_parser.rs.
In Desktop, mark repaired tool cards with a 'repaired' chip, and record per-model repair and failure rates in crates/tui/src/scorecard.rs so the model picker can warn about unreliable models. Make sure Desktop-created num_ctx variants inherit from the official tag (`from`) so Ollama's model-specific parser/renderer still applies, and check that /api/show still lists 'tools'.
date: Ollama parsers current Oct 2026; Ollama streaming tool calls 2025-05-28; AI SDK docs current

name: Lean tool surface and small-model-friendly ACI (tool-count reduction plus deferred tools)
what: Small models choose tools far worse when many are offered, and every tool schema eats tokens from a 4k–32k window. Exposing about 8 core tools with flat schemas, keeping the rest behind a search meta-tool, and using SWE-agent-style concise outputs makes local models markedly more reliable.
concrete_claims:
- Less-is-More (arXiv 2411.15399, Nov 2024) dynamically reduces the tools offered to the model. It cut execution time by up to 70% and power by up to 40% on edge devices (BFCL/GeoEngine) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.15399). CarbonCall (arXiv 2504.20348) notes that smaller edge models struggle to pick the right tool from a large set (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20348).
- mini-SWE-agent has about 100 lines of agent code and bash only. It scores >74% on SWE-bench Verified, and the SWE-bench 'Bash Only' leaderboard runs every model in it (https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent, https://www.swebench.com/bash-only.html).
- SWE-agent ACI findings: a 100-line file viewer works best. The search tool lists only the files that match, because 'Showing the model more context about each match proved to be too confusing for the model'. Empty output returns an explicit 'ran successfully and did not produce any output' message (https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/blob/main/docs/background/aci.md).
- Aider: 'Above about 25k tokens of context, most models start to become distracted and become less likely to conform to their system prompt' (https://aider.chat/docs/troubleshooting/edit-errors.html).
- CodeWhale (local source) has about 95 ToolSpec implementations, a `defer_loading` flag (crates/tui/src/tools/registry.rs), and catalog meta-tools `tool_search` / `tool_search_tool_bm25` (crates/tui/src/extension_host/registry.rs).
how_we_use_it:
Add a 'Local-lean' tool profile. It is selected automatically for Ollama routes whose /api/show details.parameter_size is ≤14B, and the user can switch Lean/Full in Desktop model settings.
- Send only these core tools: read_file (100–200-line windows), search (ripgrep, returning a file list first), edit (search/replace), write_file, shell, run_verifiers, todo, and tool_search.
- Give each a one-line description and a flat JSON schema (no oneOf, no deep nesting).
- Mark everything else defer_loading=true behind tool_search (BM25).
- Slim the system prompt for this profile.
- Normalize empty outputs to an explicit success line.
Desktop shows the prefix cost, e.g. 'system+tools: 3.1k of 32k tokens', so users can see what the lean profile saves.
date: Less-is-More Nov 2024; mini-SWE-agent 2025-2026; SWE-agent ACI 2024

name: Edit-format adaptation per model and file size (whole-file vs search/replace vs line-marked diff)
what: The best edit format depends on model size. Small models rarely produce well-formed diffs but almost always produce well-formed whole files. Choosing the format per model and file size, applying edits flexibly, and tracking each model's 'well-formed edit rate' cuts failed edits sharply.
concrete_claims:
- Aider polyglot leaderboard data: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct with 'diff' scored 8.0% pass (71.6% well-formed), versus 'whole' at 16.4% (99.6% well-formed) (Dec 2024). Qwen3 32B with diff scored 40.0% (83.6% well-formed) (2025-05-08) (https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/website/_data/polyglot_leaderboard.yml).
- Aider's older edit benchmark ran small models with 'whole': Qwen2.5-Coder 3B 39.1%, 7B 57.9%, 14B 69.2%, all ~100% well-formed (Oct–Nov 2024) (https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/website/_data/edit_leaderboard.yml).
- Aider: 'Experiments where flexible patching is disabled show a 9X increase in editing errors'. Unified diffs raised GPT-4 Turbo from 20% to 61% on its laziness benchmark (https://aider.chat/docs/unified-diffs.html). The edit-format reference is at https://aider.chat/docs/more/edit-formats.html.
- Diff-XYZ (arXiv 2510.12487, Oct 2025), on 1,000 CommitPackFT edits: search-replace is generally best for diff generation with larger models. For smaller models, udiff-l (explicit ADD/DEL/CON line markers) scored best. udiff-h is much worse than udiff (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.12487).
- Kortix FastApply-1.5B and FastApply-7B (Apache-2.0, fine-tuned from Qwen2.5-Coder) merge edit snippets into full files, and community GGUFs exist (https://huggingface.co/Kortix/FastApply-7B-v1.0).
how_we_use_it:
CodeWhale's crates/tui/src/tools/file.rs already does search/replace with fuzzy normalization and old_string/new_string aliasing. Add an edit policy:
- For local models ≤8B and target files ≤~300 lines (shaders, small scripts), steer toward write_file whole-file rewrites. Rely on the syntax/verify gate (verify-on-edit item) and a Desktop diff preview to catch damage.
- Use search/replace otherwise.
- On a no-match, return the 3 closest line windows (similarity-ranked) so the model can retry with exact text instead of guessing.
- Track each model's edit well-formed rate in scorecard.rs and switch format automatically when it drops below ~85%.
- Experimental: an optional FastApply-1.5B GGUF 'apply model' for lazy '// ... existing code ...' snippets, enabled only if VRAM fits alongside the main model.
date: Aider data Oct 2024–May 2025; Diff-XYZ Oct 2025

name: Observation masking before LLM summarization (tiered context compaction)
what: Replace old tool outputs with short stubs and keep the agent's reasoning and actions. A study within SWE-agent found this cuts cost about in half while matching or slightly exceeding the solve rate of LLM summarization. It is deterministic and needs no extra model call, which suits weak local models whose summaries are unreliable.
concrete_claims:
- 'The Complexity Trap' (JetBrains/TUM, arXiv 2508.21433, Aug 2025; NeurIPS 2025 DL4Code) tested within SWE-agent on SWE-bench Verified across five model configurations. Observation masking about halves cost versus the raw agent while matching or slightly exceeding the LLM-summary solve rate, and the result generalizes to OpenHands. A masking+summary hybrid saves a further 7% and 11% versus masking-only and summary-only. The released configs use a masking window M=10 (https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/the-complexity-trap; blog Dec 2025 https://blog.jetbrains.com/research/2025/12/efficient-context-management/).
- OpenHands LLMSummarizingCondenser (Apr 2025) reports 'up to 2x per-turn API cost reduction' with equivalent or better SWE performance (https://openhands.dev/blog/openhands-context-condensensation-for-more-efficient-ai-agents, https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/context-condenser).
- Chroma 'Context Rot' (2025-07-14) tested 18 LLMs including Qwen3. They become increasingly unreliable as input length grows, even on simple tasks (https://research.trychroma.com/context-rot).
- OpenCode has a hidden 'compaction' agent that runs automatically (https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/).
how_we_use_it:
CodeWhale's compaction (crates/tui/src/compaction, SURVIVAL_CONTRACT.md) is LLM-summary based. Run by a 4B model, that is slow and lossy. Add a tier-0 'mask' pass:
- Replace tool_result blocks older than the last M=10 observations with a stub: '[elided: <tool> <args digest>, <n> lines — retrieve_tool_result id=…]'. Spilled outputs already exist via large_output_router.rs and tool_result_retrieval.rs.
- Never mask the protected last round or assistant actions.
- Mask in batches (every ~10 turns, or at 50% window pressure), not every turn, so the KV-cache prefix stays stable (prefix-caching item).
- Call the LLM summary only at ≥75% pressure (ContextBudget).
Desktop: show a context meter (raw vs masked tokens) and a 'masked N outputs' chip.
date: arXiv Aug 2025 / NeurIPS 2025 workshop; OpenHands Apr 2025; Chroma Jul 2025

name: Prefix-stable prompts plus KV/prompt-cache reuse across turns (Ollama / llama-server)
what: On a single consumer GPU, re-processing a 10–30k-token prefix every turn dominates latency. Keeping the system prompt and tool catalog byte-identical and the history append-only means only the new suffix is evaluated. Exposing the cache-hit rate makes cache-breaking regressions visible.
concrete_claims:
- Ollama's llm/server.go says: 'All GGUF models are served via the upstream llama-server subprocess' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/llm/server.go).
- llama-server reference: `cache_prompt` (default true) compares the prompt with the previous one so 'only the unseen suffix is evaluated'. `--cache-reuse N` reuses chunks via KV shifting. `--cache-ram N` sets a prompt-cache cap, default 8192 MiB. `--slot-save-path` persists slot KV to disk. `--ctx-checkpoints` defaults to 32 (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md).
- Ollama v0.33.3 (2026-09-02) added 'Report cached prompt tokens', exposed as `prompt_eval_cached_count` in the final response (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.33.3, https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md).
- Ollama v0.33.0 (2026-08-21) fixed a case where a Claude Code token-countdown system message, which Ollama moved to the front of the prompt, 'broke the KV cache on every request'. Cancelled prefills now keep their restore points (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.33.0).
- Prompt-cache size can be set with LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM (issue closed 2026-07-24 as already implemented) (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/17351).
- Ollama FAQ: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL defaults to 1, and memory scales with NUM_PARALLEL×CONTEXT_LENGTH. keep_alive defaults to 5m, and -1 keeps the model loaded (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/faq.mdx).
how_we_use_it:
CodeWhale already has crates/runtime/src/prompt_zones.rs (PinnedPrefix / AppendLog / TurnScratch with sha256 drift detection), but it is marked 'not yet wired into the request path'. Wire it for local routes:
- Freeze the system prompt and the tool list in sorted order. Keep timestamps, git status and budget warnings out of the system prompt.
- Append per-turn state only at the tail.
- Mutate history only at compaction events.
Desktop changes:
- Read `prompt_eval_cached_count` / `prompt_eval_count` (or cached-token usage, if /v1 exposes it) and show 'cache hit 96% · TTFT 0.8s' per turn. Alert when PrefixDrift fires.
- Set a long keep_alive (30m or -1) for the active model.
- On one GPU, keep sub-agents and title generation on the same model rather than swapping, because a swap evicts the whole cache.
- For power users on a raw llama-server route, expose --cache-reuse, which helps masked or compacted histories reuse the unchanged tail.
date: Ollama v0.33.0 (2026-08-21), v0.33.3 (2026-09-02); llama.cpp server README current

name: Repo map: tree-sitter symbols plus personalized PageRank in a fixed token budget
what: A compact map of the repository's most-referenced symbols gives a small-context model orientation for about 1k tokens. It reduces blind grep/read loops and helps new code reuse existing APIs. Aider pioneered it, and repository-graph augmentation (RepoGraph) improved every SWE-bench framework it was tested with.
concrete_claims:
- Aider's repo map uses tree-sitter to extract definitions and references and ranks them on a file-dependency graph. The token budget is `--map-tokens`, default 1k, and the map expands when no files are in the chat (https://aider.chat/docs/repomap.html, https://aider.chat/2023/10/22/repomap.html).
- aider/repomap.py uses personalized PageRank: files in the chat and paths matching mentioned identifiers get a personalization boost (personalize = 100/len(fnames)) (https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/repomap.py).
- RepoGraph (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2410.14684) is a plug-in repository-level code graph. It improved all four SWE-bench methods it was added to (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14684).
- Cline explores with ripgrep, AST definitions and file reads instead of a vector index (https://cline.bot/blog/why-cline-doesnt-index-your-codebase-and-why-thats-a-good-thing).
- Rust building blocks: the tree-sitter crate, tree-sitter-gdscript 6.1.0 (https://github.com/PrestonKnopp/tree-sitter-gdscript), and petgraph `page_rank(graph, damping_factor, nb_iter)`, which has no personalization argument (https://doc.servo.org/petgraph/algo/page_rank/fn.page_rank.html).
how_we_use_it:
Add a `repo_map` tool and context fragment, either in CodeWhale or precomputed by Desktop (src-tauri) and injected as project context:
- Use tree-sitter tag queries for Rust/TS/Python/GDScript, plus gdshader uniforms and functions.
- Build a file graph from identifier references and run a ~40-line personalized PageRank power iteration (petgraph has no personalization), seeded by files open or @-mentioned in the Desktop composer.
- Render signature lines in a budget that scales with the real num_ctx: about 1k tokens for 8–16k windows, 2k for 32k and above.
- Cache by mtime. Inject once after the frozen prefix and refresh only on demand, to keep the KV cache warm.
Desktop: a 'Repo map' panel showing exactly what the model sees.
date: Aider repo map 2023–2025; RepoGraph ICLR 2025

name: Phase-aware thinking-budget control (think levels per step, client-side budget cap)
what: Thinking helps on planning and debugging but wastes the token budget and can loop on routine tool steps, especially in 4B models. Newer Ollama exposes each model's thinking controls, and llama-server supports true token budgets. CodeWhale should switch thinking per step instead of per session.
concrete_claims:
- Ollama `think` accepts a boolean or a level ('low','medium','high','max') (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md). Since v0.34.3 (2026-09-19), `/api/show` returns `thinking: {values, default}`. 'Numbers are not supported'. Output comes back in `message.thinking` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/capabilities/thinking.mdx, https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.34.3).
- /v1 accepts `reasoning_effort` / `reasoning.effort`. 'none' requests false, 'minimal' maps to low, and 'xhigh'/'ultra' map to max (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api/openai-compatibility.mdx).
- When streaming with tools, gather all `thinking`, `content` and `tool_calls` chunks and send them back together in the follow-up request (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/capabilities/tool-calling.mdx).
- llama-server `--reasoning-budget N` takes -1 (unrestricted), 0 (end immediately) or N>0 (a token budget). `--reasoning-budget-message` sets text injected at the cutoff. Per request, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` is available (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md). Issue #22717 reports the budget message not appearing, after which the model 'tends to start to loop' (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/22717).
- s1 (arXiv 2501.19393, Jan 2025): 'budget forcing', i.e. forcing end-of-thinking or appending 'Wait', controls test-time compute (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393). The Qwen3 Technical Report (arXiv 2505.09388) introduces a thinking-budget mechanism (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388).
how_we_use_it:
CodeWhale has crates/tui/src/reasoning_preference.rs and auto_reasoning.rs.
- Desktop fills each model's effort picker from /api/show `thinking.values` instead of hardcoding.
- Default local policy: think=false/low for routine tool steps (read, search, an edit that follows an approved plan). Use high for planning, after a failed verify gate (verify-on-edit item), and for final review.
- Add a client-side cap for Ollama, since it has no numeric budgets. Count streamed thinking tokens and, past the budget (e.g. ~1.5k for 4B models, configurable), abort and re-issue with think=false and 'Answer now with the next action'.
- Show thinking tokens and time separately in the turn footer.
date: Ollama v0.34.3 (2026-09-19); llama.cpp reasoning budget 2025–2026; s1 Jan 2025

name: Plan→Act split (architect/editor) tuned for a single GPU
what: Separating 'decide what to change' from 'emit the exact edits' lets each phase use the best setting: thinking-heavy planning, then lean, precise acting. Aider's architect/editor pairing produced SOTA results and roughly tripled pass rate for a local-class model pair. Cline and OpenCode ship Plan/Act modes as first-class features.
concrete_claims:
- Aider Architect/Editor (2024-09-26): o1-preview as Architect with DeepSeek or o1-mini as Editor reached the SOTA score of 85% (https://aider.chat/2024/09/26/architect.html).
- Aider polyglot (2025-03-07): QwQ-32B architect + Qwen2.5-Coder editor scored 26.2%, versus Qwen2.5-Coder-32B alone at 16.4% (whole) and 8.0% (diff) (https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/website/_data/polyglot_leaderboard.yml).
- Cline Plan mode 'can read your codebase, run searches, and discuss strategy, but cannot modify any files or execute commands'. Plan and Act can use separate models ('Use different models for Plan and Act') (https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/docs/core-workflows/plan-and-act.mdx).
- OpenCode ships built-in Build and Plan primary agents, with Plan's edit and bash permissions set to ask (https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/).
how_we_use_it:
CodeWhale already has Plan/Act/Operate modes (HookEvent::ModeChange) plus crates/tui/src/tools/plan.rs and workflow_plan_approval.rs. Desktop adds per-mode presets:
- Plan: the same local model with think=high and read-only tools. Output is a structured plan (constrained-decoding item): files, steps, and the verify command for each step.
- Act: think off/low, the Local-lean tool profile, and one plan step per turn. After 2 consecutive failed verify gates it returns to Plan automatically.
A two-model architect/editor mode is offered only when /api/ps size_vram plus nvidia-smi free memory show both models fit. Otherwise use the same model with different think levels, which avoids a reload and keeps the KV cache.
date: Aider architect 2024-09-26; polyglot data 2025-03-07; Cline/OpenCode docs current

name: Constrained decoding for internal structured sub-calls (not for reasoning)
what: Use JSON-schema/grammar-constrained decoding for CodeWhale's machine-consumed outputs: compaction summaries, plans, verdicts, titles and routing. These then always parse, even from a 4B model. Leave reasoning and main agent turns unconstrained, because strict formats measurably hurt reasoning.
concrete_claims:
- 'Let Me Speak Freely?' (arXiv 2408.02442, EMNLP 2024 Industry): format restrictions, especially JSON-mode constrained decoding, degrade reasoning, and stricter constraints degrade it more. They can improve classification (https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.02442).
- CRANE (ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.09061) lets reasoning run unconstrained and constrains the output. It reports up to 10 percentage points over baselines on GSM-symbolic and FOLIO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09061).
- JSONSchemaBench (arXiv 2501.10868, Jan 2025) uses 10K real-world schemas to compare Guidance, Outlines, llama.cpp, XGrammar, OpenAI and Gemini (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.10868).
- Ollama v0.34.4 (2026-09-23): 'Structured outputs on thinking models now apply in a single pass', plus 'Updated llama.cpp, MLX, and XGrammar' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.34.4).
- llama.cpp converts json_schema to GBNF with stated gaps: prefixItems broken, patterns must be ^…$ anchored, no patternProperties/uniqueItems/not/if-then-else (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/grammars/README.md). The optional llguidance build (-DLLAMA_LLGUIDANCE=ON) computes a token mask in about 50 μs on average, p99 0.5 ms (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/llguidance.md).
how_we_use_it:
Route CodeWhale's non-conversational sub-calls through native POST /api/chat with `format: <JSON schema>`. This can live in the Desktop shim or as an Ollama-native path in CodeWhale's client. Targets:
- compaction summaries (schema = the SURVIVAL_CONTRACT.md 'survive' fields)
- the plan object for Plan mode
- todo updates
- verifier verdict classification
- commit messages, session titles and routing decisions
Keep `think` on where useful, so reasoning goes to message.thinking and only the final answer is constrained (CRANE-style). Keep schemas flat, avoid the unsupported keywords, and repeat the schema in the prompt as Ollama's docs advise. Never set `format` on main agent turns.
date: Ollama v0.34.4 (2026-09-23); CRANE ICML 2025; JSONSchemaBench Jan 2025

name: Optional local semantic code search (small embedding model, hybrid with ripgrep)
what: An opt-in background index of AST-chunked code, embedded with a sub-1B local model and fused with keyword search. It helps small models that explore poorly find the right files in one step. Leading agents (Cline, Continue) moved away from pure RAG, so this should supplement grep, not replace it.
concrete_claims:
- Qwen3-Embedding (Jun 2025) comes in 0.6B/4B/8B with 32K sequence length and Matryoshka (MRL) dimensions. It is instruction-aware, with instructions typically adding 1–5%. On MTEB-Code retrieval over the top-100 from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (75.41), Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B scores 73.42 (lower), 4B 81.20 and 8B 81.22 (https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Embedding).
- EmbeddingGemma 2 (released 2026-10-06) is about 740M parameters with a 270M text+code core, 768-d vectors (MRL down to 128), an 8,192-token context and an Apache-2.0 license. Secondary coverage reports 78.68 on MTEB code (https://siliconangle.com/2026/10/06/google-expands-embeddinggemma-beyond-text-to-images-audio-and-video/). Ollama v0.40.4-rc1 (2026-10-12) updated llama.cpp for EmbeddingGemma 2 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases).
- Ollama /api/embed supports `dimensions` and `truncate` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md). Ollama documents no rerank endpoint. llama-server provides /v1/rerank with `--reranking` plus `--embedding --pooling rank` (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md).
- Cline does not index codebases (chunking breaks code logic; staleness; IP) (https://cline.bot/blog/why-cline-doesnt-index-your-codebase-and-why-thats-a-good-thing). Continue deprecated @Codebase in favor of agent-mode codebase awareness (https://docs.continue.dev/reference/deprecated-codebase).
how_we_use_it:
Add a Desktop background indexer (src-tauri), off by default:
- Chunk by tree-sitter function/class, reusing the repo-map parser.
- Embed via Ollama /api/embed with qwen3-embedding:0.6b or embeddinggemma at 256–512 dims, using a task instruction for queries.
- Store in a per-workspace SQLite vector table and update incrementally from git diff and mtime.
- Expose a `semantic_search(query,k)` tool that returns file:line ranges, fused with ripgrep hits by reciprocal-rank fusion.
Skip the 0.6B reranker, which hurt code retrieval in Qwen's own table. Offer the 4B reranker only via llama-server when VRAM allows. Index while idle, with a short keep_alive on the embed model so VRAM goes back to the chat model. For ≤8B models, optionally auto-attach the top 5 locations to the first turn.
date: Qwen3-Embedding Jun 2025; EmbeddingGemma 2 2026-10-06; Ollama v0.40.4-rc1 2026-10-12

name: Verifier-guided test-time scaling (best-of-N candidate fixes in worktrees)
what: When a small model keeps failing a checkable task (shader doesn't compile, test fails), sample several candidate edits and let the deterministic verifier pick. Combining execution-based and model-based verifiers beats either one alone. This trades local GPU time, which is free, for reliability.
concrete_claims:
- R2E-Gym (arXiv 2504.07164, Apr 2025; NeurIPS 2025): execution-based and execution-free verifiers each saturate around 42–43%. The hybrid reaches 51% on SWE-bench Verified, a new open-weight SOTA at the time (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07164).
- Agentless filters multiple candidate patches with regression tests and generated reproduction tests, then re-ranks them (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01489).
- Ollama FAQ: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL defaults to 1, and memory scales with NUM_PARALLEL×CONTEXT_LENGTH (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/faq.mdx).
- Ollama v0.35.0 (2026-09-28) added decision models via `/v1/systemone`. Question types are `choice`, `noul` ('Return the probability that a condition is true') and `score`, and responses carry probabilities instead of text, e.g. model `nimble` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.35.0).
how_we_use_it:
Add a 'Try N fixes' action in Desktop. It appears automatically after the verify-on-edit retry cap is hit, e.g. a .gdshader still failing check-shader.ps1 after 3 attempts.
- Generate N=2–4 candidate edits at temperature ~0.7, sequentially, or with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2 at a reduced num_ctx.
- Apply each in a temporary git worktree.
- Run the verifier map on each and keep only the passing candidates.
- Break ties by smallest diff, or with a cheap judge: the same model with a constrained yes/no verdict, or experimentally an Ollama decision model's `noul` probability for 'this diff fixes the reported error'.
- Show the survivors side by side for the user to pick.
This fits short compile-checkable artifacts best: shaders, small scripts, single failing tests.
date: R2E-Gym Apr 2025; Agentless Jul 2024; Ollama v0.35.0 2026-09-28

name: Client-executed dynamic tools (CodeWhale Runtime API): desktop-native tools for Godot, GPU, screenshots
what: CodeWhale's app-server lets a client register its own tools on a thread or turn. The model calls them, the Runtime emits an SSE event, and the desktop runs the tool locally and posts the result back, which can be text or images. This is the most direct way to give a small local model reliable, deterministic tools without writing an MCP server.
date: Present in CodeWhale 0.10.2 (2026-10-10); source checked at commit 182bafe (2026-10-13)
concrete_claims: POST /v1/threads and POST /v1/threads/{id}/turns accept `dynamic_tools: [{namespace?, name, description, input_schema, defer_loading?}]` (DynamicToolSpec; ${SRC}/crates/protocol/src/runtime/mod.rs:195-217; test ${SRC}/crates/tui/src/runtime_api/tests.rs:10320 `create_thread_accepts_dynamic_tools_and_environments`, :10409 `start_turn_accepts_dynamic_tools_and_environment_id`). When the model calls one, the Runtime emits SSE `tool_call.requested` with {thread_id, turn_id, call_id, namespace, tool, arguments} (${SRC}/crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:19326-19346). The client answers with `POST /v1/threads/{thread_id}/turns/{turn_id}/tool-calls/{call_id}/result` and body `{success, content:[{type:"input_text",text}|{type:"input_image",image_url}]}` (mod.rs:253-270). Exactly one of `tool_call.resolved`, `tool_call.timeout` or `tool_call.canceled` becomes durable, and 202 means the result was durably accepted (${SRC}/docs/RUNTIME_API.md:1425-1447, https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/RUNTIME_API.md). Dynamic tools are NOT available over the ACP transport (RUNTIME_API.md:718). Today the desktop sends no dynamic_tools and limits `allowed_tools` to LITE_TOOLS = [read, write, edit, bash, todo_write] (/home/user/LOCAL_AGENT_PROJECT/codewhale-desktop/src/lib/tools.ts:68; src/store/app.ts newThread/sendPrompt).
how_we_use_it: Add a `desktop` namespace of Tauri-implemented tools to the newThread/sendPrompt body. (1) `godot.check_shader {path}` runs tools\check-shader.ps1 with the custom Godot 4.8 binary and returns COMPILES or the compiler errors as input_text. It replaces the fragile 'bash + PowerShell 5.1 quoting' loop from AGENTS.md with one schema-validated call. (2) `godot.render_preview {path, frames}` renders the shader to a PNG and returns it as an input_image data URL, so a vision model in Ollama can look at the result. (3) `system.vram` / `ollama.ps` report free VRAM and loaded models, so the agent can reason about context size. Handle `tool_call.requested` in src/hooks/useBootstrap.ts and src/store/threads.ts, and show a 'running locally' card with a Cancel button that posts `{success:false}`. Put the namespaced names into allowed_tools; check whether the Runtime expects the `<namespace>::<name>` spelling. Keep descriptions short, because each tool's schema costs context on a 32k model.

name: Checkpoints / Rewind UI over CodeWhale's side-git snapshots
what: CodeWhale already keeps side-git workspace snapshots and exposes conversation-and-code rewind routes. The desktop only offers 'fork' today. A Claude-Code-style rewind menu on every user turn would make experimenting with weak local models safe: try, rewind, retry.
date: CodeWhale 0.10.2 (2026-10-10); Claude Code checkpointing docs (current, 2026)
concrete_claims: Routes: `POST /v1/threads/{id}/fork-at-turn {turn_id}` keeps that turn and everything before it, and returns `original_user_text` for the composer; it never rolls back files. `POST /v1/threads/{id}/patch-undo {depth}` rolls back the files the dropped turns changed, then forks, and returns `patch_result{files_restored, summary, snapshot_label}`. `POST /v1/threads/{id}/file-revert {path, snapshot_id, expected_hash}` restores exactly one file. `POST /v1/threads/{id}/retry {depth, prompt}`. `GET /v1/snapshots?limit=` and `POST /v1/snapshots/{id}/restore` take a `pre-restore:` safety snapshot first and return 409 while a turn is active (${SRC}/docs/RUNTIME_API.md:1210-1214, 1493-1524). Snapshot config: `[snapshots].enabled` (default true) and `max_age_days` (default 7); snapshots are stored in `~/.codewhale/snapshots/<project_hash>/<worktree_hash>/.git` and never in the project's own .git (${SRC}/docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2552-2558). For comparison, Claude Code's /rewind offers 'Restore code and conversation / Restore conversation / Restore code / Summarize from here', and it does NOT track files changed by Bash commands (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing). The desktop already handles `turn.workspace_snapshot` and `thread.forked` events (codewhale-desktop/src/store/threads.ts:222,277) but calls only forkThread.
how_we_use_it: Add a hover menu on each user message in src/components/chat/Turn.tsx with four actions. 'Rewind conversation' calls fork-at-turn with that turn_id and puts the original text back in the composer. 'Rewind conversation + files' calls patch-undo with a depth computed by the server, not counted in the client, and shows files_restored. 'Retry with another model' calls retry. 'Restore this file' sits in the DiffView and calls file-revert. Add a 'Snapshots' tab to the Inspector that lists GET /v1/snapshots with a guarded Restore button, disabled while a turn runs (the server returns 409). Map 409 'already has an active turn' to a clear toast. For a Godot workspace on F:, show the snapshot age limit and add a settings toggle for max_age_days.

name: Server-side approval policy: permission posture, scoped grants, permissions.toml and Auto-Review instead of client auto-approve
what: The desktop currently auto-approves by bare tool name on the client, so 'bash' means every command. CodeWhale already has a layered, monotonic authorization pipeline: hooks, typed rules, a deterministic Auto-Review floor plus a model guardian, repo law, and session grants scoped to a command family. The desktop should drive that pipeline instead of bypassing it.
date: CodeWhale 0.10.2 (2026-10-10); Claude Code auto mode: engineering post 2026-03-25, made the default in August 2026
concrete_claims: Desktop auto-approve: useBootstrap.ts:57-64 calls `decideApproval(...true)` whenever `settings.autoApprove[tool]` is set (/home/user/LOCAL_AGENT_PROJECT/codewhale-desktop/src/hooks/useBootstrap.ts). Runtime: `POST /v1/threads` accepts `permission_posture` ("ask", "auto-review", ...), normalized to `auto_review` (${SRC}/crates/tui/src/runtime_api/tests.rs:10361-10375). `POST /v1/approvals/{id} {decision, remember}`: with remember=true it records a session grant scoped to a command family (for example `git status` with value-free options) or to the exact command. The Runtime emits `approval.grant_added` and supports `DELETE /v1/threads/{id}/approval-grants/{grant_id}`. `GET /v1/approvals?limit=` returns a redacted history with outcome and decided_by (user, session_rule, posture, host) (${SRC}/docs/RUNTIME_API.md:1338-1407). The authorization order has 9 layers; hooks resolve deny > ask > allow, and typed rules in `permissions.toml` rank User > Agent > BuiltinDefault (${SRC}/docs/AUTHORIZATION_ORDER.md). `[auto_review]` allow/block rules match `tool` and/or `action_kind` (read, write, shell, external, publish, destructive). Fallback holds go to ONE stateless guardian model call, and anything that fails fails closed (${SRC}/docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2362-2407; ${SRC}/docs/MODES.md:195-220). Industry context: Anthropic's classifier-based auto mode (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-auto-mode) became Claude Code's default in August 2026 (https://9to5mac.com/2026/08/14/psa-claude-code-enabling-auto-mode-as-default-next-week-anthropic-says/).
how_we_use_it: (1) Replace the per-tool autoApprove map with a posture chip in the Toolbar (Ask / Auto-Review / Full Access). It sends `permission_posture` on POST /v1/threads and PATCH. (2) The 'Allow for session' button already sends remember=true; add a 'Granted' list in the Inspector that reads `approval_grants[]` from thread detail and offers Revoke. (3) Add an 'Approvals log' panel backed by GET /v1/approvals. (4) Add a Settings page that edits typed `permissions.toml` rules, for example allow `git status` / `git diff`, deny `Remove-Item -Recurse` outside the workspace, and ask for `git push`. Add `[auto_review]` allow rules for action_kind=read. (5) Caveat for the UI: on one GPU the Auto-Review guardian is an extra inference call on the same local model, and a 4B model is a weak safety judge. Default to Ask plus deterministic rules, and offer Auto-Review only for larger models.

name: Agent Skills (SKILL.md open standard): skills manager, explicit activation and auto-suggest for small models
what: Agent Skills is the cross-vendor SKILL.md format (published December 2025) and loads in stages: metadata first, then the body, then resources. CodeWhale discovers SKILL.md from its own roots and from compatible roots, and exposes listing, detail, install, trust, audit and update through the Runtime API. The desktop has no skills UI, although the user's Godot workflow depends on a `godot-shaders` skill.
date: Spec published 2025-12-18; CodeWhale 0.10.2 (2026-10-10)
concrete_claims: Spec (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/docs/specification.mdx): required `name` (1-64 chars: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; must match the directory) and `description` (1-1024 chars); optional `license`, `compatibility` (1-500 chars), `metadata`, and `allowed-tools` (experimental). Folders are scripts/, references/ and assets/. Disclosure is staged: metadata about 100 tokens, body under 5000 tokens recommended, SKILL.md under 500 lines. Validate with `skills-ref validate ./my-skill`. CodeWhale: routes `GET /v1/skills`, `GET /v1/skills/{name}` (full body; advertised as `capabilities.skill_detail` on /v1/runtime/info), `/v1/skills/install`, `/{name}/trust`, `/{name}/audit`, `/{name}/update` (${SRC}/docs/RUNTIME_API.md:1777-1798; route list in ${SRC}/crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs). Writable roots are `<workspace>/.codewhale/skills/` and `~/.codewhale/skills/`. Read-only compatible roots include `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills`. Workspace roots load only once the workspace is trusted (${SRC}/docs/SKILLS.md). `invocation: explicit-only` or `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps a skill out of the model catalogue. CodeWhale only WARNS on `allowed-tools`, `model`, `context` and `agent`, which grant no authority (${SRC}/docs/SKILLS.md:141-170).
how_we_use_it: (1) A 'Skills' side panel in src/components/overlays/SidePanels.tsx lists GET /v1/skills with source, enabled and trust badges, offers Install from a GitHub URL or folder, and shows audit output. (2) In the Composer, typing '/' or '$' opens a skill picker. Choosing a skill fetches GET /v1/skills/{name} and prepends an activation instruction to the next prompt, the same way TUI `/skill <name>` does. This matters because a 4B model often fails to call load_skill on its own. (3) Auto-suggest: when the prompt or an attached file mentions `.gdshader`, show a chip 'Use godot-shaders skill'. (4) Show the token cost of the skill catalogue in the context meter, and offer to mark rarely used skills `invocation: explicit-only` to save prompt budget on 32k models. (5) Warn in the UI that `allowed-tools` in imported Claude skills is ignored by CodeWhale.

name: MCP server manager in the desktop (CRUD, tool allowlists, OAuth, registry) with a Godot MCP preset
what: CodeWhale's Runtime API can create, update, enable, disable and reconnect MCP servers and list their tools, with per-server tool allowlists and environment-backed credentials. The desktop has no MCP UI. With small local models, keeping the exposed tool catalogue minimal is the key to reliable tool calling.
date: CodeWhale 0.10.2 (2026-10-10): servers now connect at session start unless `lazy = true`; MCP Registry in preview since 2025-09-08, API v0.1 frozen 2025-10-24
concrete_claims: Routes: `GET/POST /v1/apps/mcp/servers`, `PATCH /v1/apps/mcp/servers/{name}`, `/enable`, `/disable`, `/reconnect`, `/v1/apps/mcp/imports`, `GET /v1/apps/mcp/tools?server=` (${SRC}/crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2658-2687). The write body (McpServerWriteRequest, runtime_api.rs:1347-1400) has command, args, env, url, transport ("sse" or "streamable_http"), connect_timeout, execute_timeout, read_timeout, enabled, required, enabled_tools (allowlist), disabled_tools, env_headers, bearer_token_env_var, scopes and oauth_resource. CodeWhale 0.10.2 CHANGELOG: servers connect at session start unless `lazy = true`, and `/mcp reload` redials (${SRC}/CHANGELOG.md:10-45). There is a built-in registry sync against `https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers` (${SRC}/crates/tui/src/tools/mcp_registry.rs:15,360); that registry is still a preview with breaking changes possible (search: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry). Godot preset: Coding-Solo/godot-mcp (MIT, about 6.1k stars). It runs with `npx @coding-solo/godot-mcp`, honours env `GODOT_PATH`, and exposes run_project, get_debug_output, stop_project, launch_editor, create_scene, add_node and other tools (https://github.com/Coding-Solo/godot-mcp).
how_we_use_it: Add a 'MCP' tab in SettingsPanel. It lists servers with connected / auth_required / error status, has add and edit forms for stdio or URL servers that write through POST/PATCH, Enable, Disable and Reconnect buttons, and a 'Login' action for OAuth. It never stores secrets in plain text: env_headers and bearer_token_env_var reference environment variables. Each server row has a tool checklist bound to `enabled_tools`, and the tool count is shown against the model's context budget. Ship a one-click 'Godot' preset: `npx @coding-solo/godot-mcp` with GODOT_PATH=F:\PROJECTS\godot-hd\engine\bin\godot.windows.editor.x86_64.exe and only run_project, get_debug_output and stop_project enabled. Default to `lazy=true` so a missing Node install does not slow session start. Add a 'Browse registry' dialog that uses the registry tool or a direct call to the registry.

name: Windows command sandboxing gap: honest status now, real isolation later (restricted token/ACL, LPAC AppContainer, Windows Sandbox)
what: On Windows, CodeWhale runs model-proposed shell commands with NO OS sandbox. It only places them in a Job Object for kill-on-close and memory limits. Approvals are the only control. Proven Windows designs exist: OpenAI Codex uses a restricted-token plus ACL sandbox, CodeWhale's own extension host already runs plugins in an LPAC AppContainer, and Windows Sandbox has a CLI.
date: CodeWhale docs at 2026-10-13; Codex Windows sandbox issues open as of 2026-10-09; wsb CLI ships with Windows 11 24H2
concrete_claims: CodeWhale: 'The Windows command path currently reports no OS sandbox'. The source tree has only a future Job Object helper contract, with no read-only/workspace-write enforcement, network blocking, or restricted-token/AppContainer isolation (${SRC}/docs/SANDBOX.md, Windows section). Shell children are put in a Job with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (${SRC}/crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs:37-40,700-704), and process_tree.rs can add JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PROCESS_MEMORY (lines 579-599). The extension host already uses 'a freshly created LPAC AppContainer with no network capabilities' and verifies the token (${SRC}/crates/tui/src/extension_host/supervisor.rs:49-54; windows.rs uses CreateAppContainerProfile). An external option is `sandbox_backend = "opensandbox"` with `sandbox_url`; unsupported backends refuse shell (SANDBOX.md). Codex: the crate `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs` (https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs; repo licence Apache-2.0) is configured with `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"|"unelevated"`. Issue #52427 (opened 2026-10-09, still open) reports elevated setup failing on an ACL refresh with codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2 (https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52427). Design write-up: https://openai.com/index/building-codex-windows-sandbox/. Windows Sandbox CLI `wsb` (start / exec / share / stop, `--raw` JSON) is available from Windows 11 24H2 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-isolation/windows-sandbox/windows-sandbox-cli).
how_we_use_it: Short term (S): read `codewhale doctor --json` (sandbox_available) at startup and show a red 'No OS sandbox (Windows)' chip in the StatusBar. While it shows, block 'Full Access' unless the user confirms, and default new threads to Ask. Medium term (M): add an optional 'Disposable run' button that copies the workspace into a Windows Sandbox (`wsb start`, then `wsb share --allow-write` on a scratch copy, then `wsb exec`) for risky scripts. This cannot run the Godot GPU editor, so it is for build and test scripts only. Long term (L, upstream PR to CodeWhale): implement the Windows `workspace-write` wrapper, either by reusing the LPAC AppContainer code already in extension_host/windows.rs (grant the AppContainer SID on the workspace; risk: dev tools and the GPU may break under LPAC) or by adopting Codex's Apache-2.0 restricted-token plus synthetic-SID ACL approach, while learning from its open setup bugs. The OpenSandbox/Docker backend is not suitable for the Godot loop, because the Windows Godot binary cannot run in a Linux container.

name: MCP spec 2026-07-28 (stateless, MRTR elicitation) compatibility, and an elicitation UI
what: MCP 2026-07-28 is the current stable spec revision. It removes the initialize handshake and sessions and replaces server-initiated elicitation, sampling and roots with Multi Round-Trip Requests (`input_required`). CodeWhale's native MCP client still sends `initialize` at 2025-06-18, and it declares NO client capabilities, so servers can neither elicit input from the user nor talk to modern-only peers.
date: MCP 2026-07-28 stable released 2026-07-28 (RC 2026-05-29); MCP Apps and tasks are extensions
concrete_claims: 2026-07-28 changes: initialize and `Mcp-Session-Id` removed (SEP-2575/2567); `server/discover` is a MUST on servers; `InputRequiredResult` with `inputRequests`, answered by a retry carrying `inputResponses` (SEP-2322); `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers required on Streamable HTTP (SEP-2243); `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` on list results (SEP-2549); tasks moved to the `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension (SEP-2663); Roots, Sampling and Logging deprecated, as is the HTTP+SSE transport (SEP-2577/2596) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx; https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/). Versioning: a modern-only server SHOULD list supported versions in its error to `initialize`; stdio clients SHOULD probe `server/discover` first (.../2026-07-28/basic/versioning.mdx). Elicitation: form mode takes a flat schema of primitives (string with email, uri, date or date-time format; number; boolean; single- or multi-select enum); URL mode requires consent and showing the full URL; actions are accept, decline or cancel; capability is declared under `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` as `elicitation.form` and `elicitation.url` (.../2026-07-28/client/elicitation.mdx). CodeWhale: `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2025-06-18"`; the client also accepts "2025-11-25", "2025-03-26" and "2024-11-05" (${SRC}/crates/tui/src/mcp.rs:56-73); `"capabilities": {}` because 'we offer none of the client features yet' (mcp.rs:2166-2171). The protocol already defines `ElicitationRequest {server_name, request_id, prompt}` (${SRC}/crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:1105-1110), and an execpolicy flag `mcp_elicitations` exists.
how_we_use_it: (1) Desktop, now: in the MCP tab, show each server's error from /v1/apps/mcp/servers. Detect 'unsupported protocol version' and explain that the server is MCP 2026-07-28-only and needs a newer CodeWhale. (2) Upstream issue or PR to CodeWhale: add a `server/discover` probe and a 2026-07-28 path, declare `elicitation.form`, and forward `input_required` elicitations as a Runtime event and approval-like route. (3) Desktop, after that lands: reuse the existing UserInputCard (src/components/chat/UserInputCard.tsx), which already renders request_user_input questions, to render elicitation forms from the flat primitive schema. Render URL mode as a consent dialog that shows the full URL and domain and opens it in the system browser through tauri-plugin-opener, never in the webview. Ignore the deprecated sampling and roots.

name: Parallel lanes: git worktree isolation and a sub-agent run panel, tuned to one GPU
what: CodeWhale sub-agents can run in an isolated git worktree and branch, and their runs can be inspected and cancelled through the Runtime API. The desktop can also start isolated sessions itself by pointing a new thread at a worktree. On one consumer GPU, Ollama serialises requests by default, so parallelism needs explicit UI limits.
date: CodeWhale 0.10.2 (2026-10-10); Ollama FAQ (current)
concrete_claims: Sub-agents: `worktree: true` creates a fresh worktree and branch (default `codex/agent-<name>-<id>`, checkout under `.codewhale-worktrees/`), plus `worktree_branch`, `worktree_base` and `worktree_path`. `write_authority: worktree_write` requires real isolation (${SRC}/docs/SUBAGENTS.md:190-237). Sub-agent inspection routes: `GET /v1/agent-runs`, `GET /v1/agent-runs/{run_id}` and `POST /v1/agent-runs/{run_id}/cancel`, which return 200, 202, 404 or 409 (${SRC}/docs/RUNTIME_API.md:2800-2833). `GET /v1/threads/{id}/notices` reports `subagent-terminal`, `elevation-needed` and `model-notify` (RUNTIME_API.md:1150-1165). Thread summaries include `branch`, `head`, `dirty` and `workspace` (RUNTIME_API.md:1105-1135). Git routes include /v1/git, /v1/git/branch, commit, stage, discard and push (runtime_api.rs route list). The Runtime has no 'create worktree' route for threads, but POST /v1/threads accepts `workspace`, which the desktop already sends. Ollama: `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` defaults to 1, `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` defaults to 3 per GPU, `OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE` defaults to 512, and required memory scales with NUM_PARALLEL × context length (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/faq.mdx).
how_we_use_it: (1) Add 'New isolated session' in the Sidebar. A Tauri command runs `git worktree add <repo>/../.codewhale-worktrees/<repo>/<slug> -b cw/<slug>`, then POST /v1/threads with that workspace. The session list shows the branch and a dirty badge from threads/summary. A 'Merge back / Discard' action uses /v1/git routes or `git worktree remove`. This is ideal for trying two shader approaches side by side. (2) Add a 'Workers' panel that polls GET /v1/agent-runs and the notices, with a Stop button. (3) Add a GPU-aware guard: read OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL and VRAM, warn when more than one turn or worker would queue on the same GPU, and default the maximum sub-agent concurrency to 1 for local models.

name: Hooks: read-only panel and Windows-ready templates (tool_call_before gate, shell_env)
what: CodeWhale hooks are shell commands that run at lifecycle events. On Runtime API threads, which is what the desktop drives, four of them fire: tool_call_before (can allow, deny or ask, rewrite input, or add context), shell_env (injects environment variables), tool_call_after and on_error. The Runtime lists the effective hook set and any load problems through a route.
concrete_claims: Scope table: Runtime API threads (desktop app, web) fire `tool_call_before`, `shell_env`, `tool_call_after` and `on_error`; there are 15 events in total, and UI events such as session_start and waiting_for_user fire only in the TUI (${SRC}/docs/HOOKS.md:14-27, 231-249). Config: `[hooks] enabled`, `[[hooks.hooks]] event/command/name/timeout_secs/background/continue_on_error/condition`. Commands run with `cmd /C` on Windows. `default_timeout_secs` OVERRIDES every per-hook timeout (HOOKS.md:63-96). tool_call_before stdout JSON is `{decision: allow|deny|ask, reason, updatedInput (at most 32 KiB), additionalContext}`, capped at 2000 chars per field and 8000 per call. Exit code 2 is a hard deny, and a strict hook that gives no verdict fails closed (HOOKS.md:445-490). Route `GET /v1/hooks[?thread_id=]` returns `{workspace, enabled, hooks:[{name,event,command(masked),background,timeout_secs,source}], problems}` (${SRC}/docs/RUNTIME_API.md:1954-1966). Project hooks come from a trusted `.codewhale/hooks.toml`.
how_we_use_it: Add a 'Hooks' section in Settings that renders GET /v1/hooks (source badges global / plugin / project, plus the problems list) with an 'Open config' button. Offer templates written as PowerShell called through `cmd /C powershell -NoProfile -File ...`. (a) A shell_env hook that exports GODOT_BIN=F:\PROJECTS\godot-hd\engine\bin\godot.windows.editor.x86_64.exe, so prompts and skills never hard-code the path. (b) A tool_call_before gate that denies `Remove-Item -Recurse`, `format` and `git push --force` outside the workspace, giving a reason the model can read. (c) A tool_call_before hook on write/edit of `*.gdshader` that adds additionalContext reminding the model to run check_shader. Warn in the UI that session-level events (waiting_for_user, session_idle) do not fire on desktop threads; the desktop already gets those states from SSE.

name: AGENTS.md (AAIF standard): instruction-sources inspector and editor
what: AGENTS.md is the cross-agent project-instructions convention. It is now governed by the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation together with MCP and goose. CodeWhale loads AGENTS.md as its project instructions and exposes the sources it actually loaded through a route. The user's repo already has an AGENTS.md with Russian-language and PowerShell 5.1 rules.
date: AAIF launched 2025-12-09; 247 member organisations per the 2026-08-13 Linux Foundation release
concrete_claims: AAIF hosts MCP (contributed by Anthropic), goose (Block) and AGENTS.md (OpenAI) (https://sdtimes.com/ai/linux-foundation-forms-agentic-ai-foundation-to-be-new-home-for-mcp-goose-and-agents-md/; https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/agentic-ai-foundation-welcomes-57-new-members-gaining-major-financial-services-players-and-apac-leaders). AGENTS.md FAQ: 'The closest AGENTS.md to the edited file wins; explicit user chat prompts override everything'; no fields are required (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentsmd/agents.md/main/components/FAQSection.tsx). CodeWhale: AGENTS.md is the cross-agent project instruction file; `WHALE.md` is deprecated (${SRC}/docs/CONFIGURATION.md:66-154). `GET /v1/workspace/instructions` returns the effective instruction sources, whether a generated fallback is in use, and warnings (${SRC}/crates/tui/src/runtime_api/workspace.rs:863-890; route at runtime_api.rs:2408). `[context].project_pack` (default false) adds a directory listing to the stable prefix and is described as 'useful for weak tool-calling models' (CONFIGURATION.md:2559-2563).
how_we_use_it: Add a 'Context' tab in the Inspector that calls GET /v1/workspace/instructions. It lists every loaded file (global, then repo, then nested), shows the token estimate of each against /v1/threads/{id}/context window_tokens, flags warnings and a deprecated WHALE.md, and has an 'Edit' button that opens the file via PUT /v1/workspace/files. Add a 'Create AGENTS.md' wizard with sections for the build/test command, the shell (PowerShell 5.1), the language, and the Godot compile-check command, kept short for 32k models. Add a toggle for `[context].project_pack` for weak tool-calling models.

name: ACP (Agent Client Protocol): CodeWhale in Zed/JetBrains, and optionally the desktop as an ACP client for registry agents
what: ACP is a JSON-RPC-over-stdio protocol between editors and coding agents, created by Zed. A shared Zed/JetBrains agent registry launched in January 2026. CodeWhale already ships `codewhale serve --acp` with a narrowed tool profile. The desktop could also speak ACP as a client and become a front-end for other ACP agents that can use Ollama.
date: ACP registry launched 2026-01-28; ACP Schema v1.25.0 and Rust crate v1.11.0 released 09 Oct (latest)
concrete_claims: ACP stable protocol version is 1. SDKs exist for Rust (`agent-client-protocol` crate), TypeScript (`@agentclientprotocol/sdk`), Python, Kotlin and Java (https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol). Latest releases: Schema v1.25.0 and Rust crate v1.11.0 (09 Oct) stabilised session notices and compaction; v1.10.0 added an unstable subagents RFD and request-scoped MCP-over-ACP (https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol/releases). The registry repo holds 42 agents, including qwen-code, goose, opencode, codex-acp, claude-acp, gemini, mistral-vibe and kimi. It is served at `https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json`, and CI requires valid `authMethods` (https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/registry). CodeWhale is not listed. JetBrains/Zed launch: https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/01/acp-agent-registry/. CodeWhale ACP supports `initialize`, `session/new`, `session/list`, `session/load`, `session/prompt`, `session/cancel` and `session/request_permission` (allow-once only). MCP, dynamic tools, background shell and sub-agents are unavailable on that transport. 'ACP presently claims its own exclusive canonical Runtime owner. If another process holds that store, startup refuses' (${SRC}/docs/RUNTIME_API.md:696-752).
how_we_use_it: (1) Keep the desktop on `app-server --http`, which is the full API; ACP is the narrower path. (2) Add a Settings card 'Use in Zed/JetBrains' that generates the editor config snippet for `codewhale serve --acp`. Warn that it cannot run at the same time as the desktop sidecar on the same CODEWHALE_HOME, because of the exclusive runtime owner, or offer a separate home directory. (3) Optional, larger: use the Rust `agent-client-protocol` crate in src-tauri to let the desktop launch registry agents such as qwen-code, goose or opencode against the same Ollama. The existing chat, approval and diff UI would render ACP `session/update` and `session/request_permission`, which gives a multi-agent comparison mode. (4) Consider submitting CodeWhale to the ACP registry upstream (it needs `authMethods`).

name: MCP Apps (io.modelcontextprotocol/ui): interactive ui:// views inside the chat
what: MCP Apps is an official MCP extension. A tool can declare an HTML UI resource that the host renders in a sandboxed iframe, and the view talks to the host over postMessage JSON-RPC, including calling tools. It would allow rich in-chat UIs such as shader parameter sliders or scene trees. CodeWhale does not support it yet.
date: Extension spec 2026-01-26 (SEP-1865, status Final); named as an extension in the 2026-07-28 core release post
concrete_claims: Extension identifier: `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`. A tool sets `_meta.ui.resourceUri` (the flat `_meta["ui/resourceUri"]` is deprecated) and `_meta.ui.visibility` (default ["model","app"]). The resource is `ui://...` with mimeType `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. View-to-host methods: `ui/initialize`, `tools/call`, `resources/read`, `ui/message`, `ui/open-link`, `ui/request-display-mode`, `ui/update-model-context`. Host-to-view methods: `ui/notifications/tool-input`, `tool-input-partial`, `tool-result`, `tool-cancelled`, `host-context-changed`, `ui/resource-teardown`. CSP is declared in `_meta.ui.csp` (connectDomains, resourceDomains, frameDomains, baseUriDomains), with a default of `connect-src 'none'`. Iframe sandboxing is mandatory, and the host must reject app `tools/call` for tools without 'app' visibility (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/main/specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx; https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/1865). CodeWhale: no `resourceUri` or `profile=mcp-app` handling anywhere in crates/tui/src (grep over ${SRC}).
how_we_use_it: This needs upstream work first. The Runtime must pass `_meta.ui` from MCP tool definitions and results onto tool items, add a resources/read proxy route, and add an app-initiated tools/call route that goes through the normal approval pipeline. Then the desktop renders an `McpAppView` block in src/components/chat/Blocks.tsx: a sandboxed `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` with srcdoc, the CSP built from `_meta.ui.csp`, and a postMessage bridge that logs every view-initiated RPC and asks approval for tools/call. This is a nice-to-have; plan it after the items above.

name: Windows On-device Agent Registry (ODR): import system-registered MCP servers
what: Windows 11 Insider builds include an On-device Agent Registry and an `odr` CLI that lists the locally registered MCP servers, including Windows-provided agent connectors such as File Explorer. A desktop client could discover these and import them into CodeWhale's MCP config.
date: Docs ms.date 2025-10-31 (odr tool) and 2025-08-12 (host quickstart); still pre-release
concrete_claims: `odr mcp` subcommands: run, list, add `<manifest>`, remove `<server id>`, configure `<server id>`; global options -h, --version, --verbose (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-ai-docs/docs/docs/mcp/odr-tool.md). Host quickstart: run `odr.exe list`, which returns JSON with entries carrying `manifest.server.mcp_config.{command,args}`. It requires Windows build 26220.7262 or later and an MCP host with package identity (MSIX); the identity requirement is 'not enforced in the public preview release but it will be in the stable release' (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-ai-docs/docs/docs/mcp/quickstart-mcp-host.md). The docs mark the product as pre-release and subject to change.
how_we_use_it: In the MCP tab, show an 'Import from Windows' button only when `odr.exe` exists. It runs `odr.exe list` from src-tauri/src/system.rs, parses `mcp_config.command/args`, and offers each entry for POST /v1/apps/mcp/servers with `lazy=true` and a minimal enabled_tools list. Because stable ODR will require MSIX package identity, the Tauri app would need MSIX packaging to keep this working. Treat it as experimental.

name: A2A (Agent2Agent) v1.0: watch only, not needed for a local single-user client
what: A2A is the Linux Foundation protocol for agents talking to other agents over HTTP, with Agent Cards, tasks and push notifications. It reached v1.0 in 2026. It is aimed at networked, multi-vendor agent meshes, not at an editor or desktop talking to a local agent, which is the job ACP and the CodeWhale Runtime API already do.
concrete_claims: v1.0.0 (12 Mar 2026) has breaking changes: a separate application protocol and transport mappings, OAuth implicit and password flows removed, device code and PKCE added, a new `tasks/list` with filtering and pagination, and multi-tenancy on gRPC. v1.0.1 (28 May) prefers the `application/a2a+json` media type (https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/releases). Bindings are JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTPS, gRPC and HTTP+JSON/REST (https://www.turingpost.com/p/a2a). A2A has joined the AAIF stack (https://aaif.io/blog/a2a-joins-aaif). CodeWhale has no A2A implementation: a grep over ${SRC}/crates finds only an unrelated hex colour constant.
how_we_use_it: Do not build anything now. If the user later wants CodeWhale Desktop to delegate to remote or team agents, or to be called by them, the cheapest path is a small A2A adapter in src-tauri that maps an A2A task to POST /v1/threads plus turns and streams SSE back. Revisit only when there is a concrete remote-agent use case.

name: Tauri 2.12 IPC Channels (plus raw binary invoke) in place of the global `cw-stream` event
date: Tauri 2.12 announced 2026-09-26; tauri crate and @tauri-apps/api 2.12.3 published 2026-10-10
what: Tauri's `tauri::ipc::Channel<T>` is the official ordered, fast path for streaming from Rust to the webview. Events are the global, JSON-only broadcast system, and the docs say they are not built for high throughput. Raw `InvokeBody::Raw` and `ipc::Response` move binary data such as images and audio without base64 JSON.
concrete_claims: Docs: "The event system is not designed for low latency or high throughput situations" and event payloads "are always JSON strings". "Channels are designed to be fast and deliver ordered data" and are used internally for child-process output and WebSocket messages (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/develop/calling-frontend.mdx). In the implementation, each Channel message carries an `index` for ordering. JSON payloads under 8192 bytes go through eval (the code comment says this is about 2x faster than fetch on WebView2 v135); larger ones go through fetch (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/crates/tauri/src/ipc/channel.rs). Raw request bodies: `tauri::ipc::Request` with `InvokeBody::Raw`, and `invoke(cmd, Uint8Array)` from JS (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/develop/calling-rust.mdx). Current versions: tauri 2.12.3 (https://crates.io/crates/tauri), @tauri-apps/api 2.12.3 (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tauri-apps/api), with a 3.0.0-alpha.2 on the next tag. Tauri 2.12 also raises the MSRV to 1.90 and drops Windows 7 (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/blog/tauri-2.12.mdx). Optional: tauri-specta 2.0.0-rc.25 generates typed TS bindings for commands (https://crates.io/crates/tauri-specta).
how_we_use_it: Today src-tauri/src/api.rs `stream_loop` calls `app.emit("cw-stream", ...)` for every SSE event of every thread, and src/lib/tauri.ts `listen("cw-stream")` filters them in JS. Replace this with a command `subscribe_thread(thread_id, since_seq, on_event: Channel<StreamEvent>)`. Rust keeps the reqwest SSE loop, coalesces text deltas into one message every 16–33 ms, and sends them on that thread's channel. Dropping the channel ends the subscription, so there are no leaked listeners when switching threads. Keep `emit` only for low-rate global signals (runtime-status, runtime-log). Change `read_image_b64` and future audio upload to raw bytes: `invoke('attach_image', bytes)` paired with `ipc::Response`. The user sees smoother token streaming and less jank with several threads open.

name: Streamdown 2.7 + remend: incremental markdown renderer for streaming replies
date: streamdown 2.7.0 and remend 1.4.0 published 2026-09-30; @streamdown/code 2.0.0 the same day
what: Vercel's drop-in replacement for react-markdown, built for LLM streams. It splits the text into blocks with the marked lexer, memoizes each block so finished blocks never re-render, and closes unterminated `**`, code fences, links and so on with remend before parsing. It also has a caret, link-safety and rehype-harden.
concrete_claims: "A drop-in replacement for react-markdown, designed for AI-powered streaming" (https://github.com/vercel/streamdown). Block-level memoization: "Only blocks with changed content are re-rendered" (https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/memoization.mdx). Props: `parseIncompleteMarkdown` (default true), `mode: "streaming"|"static"`, `isAnimating`, `caret: "block"|"circle"`, `components`, `linkSafety` (confirmation modal on by default) (https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/tree/main/apps/website/content/docs). Peer dependency react ^18 || ^19. It depends on marked, unified and remark-gfm; @streamdown/code needs shiki ^4.4.3 (https://www.npmjs.com/package/streamdown, https://www.npmjs.com/package/@streamdown/code). Tailwind v4 needs `@source "../node_modules/streamdown/dist/*.js"` in the CSS.
how_we_use_it: src/components/chat/Markdown.tsx now runs `<ReactMarkdown remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}>` over the whole message on every token. That is O(n) re-parsing per delta, and long answers stutter. Swap it for `<Streamdown mode={streaming?'streaming':'static'} isAnimating={streaming} caret="block" components={{code: CodeBlock, a: TauriLink}} linkSafety={{enabled:false}}>`. Keep the existing CodeBlock (Shiki 4.5) and the `openUrl` link handler, and set `linkSafety` off or use `onLinkCheck`, because links are already routed through the opener plugin. Add the Tailwind `@source` line to src/index.css. Result: completed paragraphs and code blocks freeze, half-typed bold or fences render correctly, and CPU use during long generations drops.

name: Drag-and-drop and paste images for vision models, downscaled to CodeWhale's limits
date: Tauri 2.12 (2026-09-26); CodeWhale protocol limits are on current main
what: Use Tauri's native webview drag-drop event, which gives real file paths from Explorer, plus Tauri 2.12's new permission handler (ClipboardRead and Microphone kinds). Re-encode and downscale images in Rust so attachments always pass CodeWhale's server-side image validation.
concrete_claims: The CodeWhale protocol allows at most 10 images, 4 MiB per image and 5 MiB in total (MAX_RUNTIME_IMAGES, MAX_RUNTIME_IMAGE_BYTES, MAX_RUNTIME_IMAGE_TOTAL_BYTES). `prepare_runtime_images` fails with "images exceed the 5 MiB total limit" and has a decode guard of about 33.5 megapixels (https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/blob/main/crates/protocol/src/runtime/mod.rs, https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/blob/main/crates/tui/src/image_attach.rs). Tauri window config `dragDropEnabled` defaults to true: "Disabling it is required to use HTML5 drag and drop on the frontend on Windows since we replace the drag drop handler of WebView2" (@tauri-apps/cli config.schema.json, https://docs.rs/tauri/latest/tauri/webview/struct.WebviewBuilder.html#method.disable_drag_drop_handler). `getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent` delivers enter, over, drop and leave with `paths` and a physical-pixel `position` (https://v2.tauri.app/reference/javascript/api/namespacewebview/). Tauri 2.12 adds `on_permission_request` (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/blog/tauri-2.12.mdx). PermissionKind includes Microphone, Camera, Notifications, ClipboardRead and DisplayCapture (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/crates/tauri-runtime/src/webview_permissions.rs). Resizing crates: image 0.25.10, fast_image_resize 6.1.0 (https://crates.io/crates/image, https://crates.io/crates/fast_image_resize). Ollama /api/chat takes base64 `images` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md).
how_we_use_it: Existing bug: src/components/composer/Composer.tsx `addImageFile` and src-tauri/src/system.rs `read_image_b64` only check 4 MB per image and allow 10 images, so two 3 MB screenshots already exceed the server's 5 MiB total and the turn fails. Fixes: (1) Add a Rust command `prepare_image(bytes|path)` that decodes, caps the long side (for example at 1568 px), re-encodes to JPEG/WebP and returns bytes. Keep a running total under 5 MiB in the composer and show a size chip. (2) Subscribe to `getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent` in Composer: show a drop overlay on enter/over, attach image paths on drop, and turn other paths into @-mentions, matching the current picker. (3) Send bytes with raw invoke instead of a FileReader data URL. (4) Warn when the selected Ollama model lacks the vision capability. The user can drop Godot screenshots or shader output from Explorer and they always go through.

name: Desktop-shell plugin set: single-instance, window-state, tray, global-shortcut, autostart, deep-link
what: The official Tauri plugins that turn the window into a desktop tool: one instance, restored geometry, a tray icon with background mode, system-wide hotkeys (including press and release events for push-to-talk), start at login, and `codewhale://` URLs.
concrete_claims: "The Single Instance plugin must be the first one to be registered to work well" (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/plugin/single-instance.mdx). Deep links: "On Linux and Windows deep links are delivered as a command line argument to a new app process", so use `tauri-plugin-single-instance` with `features = ["deep-link"]` (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/plugin/deep-linking.mdx). Global shortcuts expose `ShortcutState::Pressed` / `Released` in Rust and `register('CommandOrControl+Shift+C', ...)` in JS (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/plugin/global-shortcut.mdx). Window state: `StateFlags`, `restoreStateCurrent`, `save_window_state` (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/plugin/window-state.mdx). Tray: `tauri = { features = ["tray-icon"] }` and `TrayIconBuilder::new()` (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/learn/system-tray.mdx). Autostart takes extra launch args such as `Some(vec!["--flag1"])` (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/blob/v2/src/content/docs/plugin/autostart.mdx). Versions are on crates.io (https://crates.io/crates/tauri-plugin-single-instance, https://crates.io/crates/tauri-plugin-global-shortcut).
how_we_use_it: src-tauri/Cargo.toml currently has only the opener and dialog plugins and `tauri` with features []. (1) single-instance first in lib.rs. src-tauri/src/runtime.rs starts `codewhale app-server` on a free port, so a second launch would spawn a second sidecar against the same state and possibly a second model load in Ollama VRAM. Instead, focus the existing window and forward argv. (2) window-state, so the 1440x900 window and sidebar size persist. (3) A tray with Show / New thread / Stop all / Quit, where closing the window hides it while turns run. (4) global-shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+Space opens a small quick-ask window, and a hold-to-talk key drives voice input. (5) autostart with `--minimized` to pre-warm the sidecar and Ollama model. (6) A `codewhale://thread/<id>` and `codewhale://new?cwd=...&prompt=...` scheme, so a Godot editor plugin, notification click or browser link can open a thread in the right workspace. GigaAM-v3 `v3_e2e_ctc` / `v3_e2e_rnnt` "support punctuation and text normalization", are MIT licensed, "win by an average margin of 70:30" against Whisper-large-v3 in LLM-judged side-by-side tests, and `.transcribe` works on audio up to 25 s (https://github.com/salute-developers/GigaAM). name: TanStack Virtual end-anchoring (`anchorTo:'end'`, `followOnAppend`) for the chat list
date: @tanstack/virtual-core 3.19.4 published 2026-10-13 (the project already resolves 3.19.4)
what: New TanStack Virtual options for chat, log and inverted feeds. The virtualizer keeps the viewport pinned to the bottom while the last item grows during streaming, keeps position when older items are prepended, and only auto-follows if the user was already at the end.

name: Shiki 4.5: @shikijs/stream incremental highlighting plus native gdshader/HLSL/WGSL grammars
date: shiki and @shikijs/stream 4.5.0 published 2026-10-01 (Shiki v4.0.0 2026-02-27)
what: `@shikijs/stream` tokenizes code as it arrives instead of re-highlighting the whole block, and ships a React `ShikiStreamRenderer`. Shiki also bundles real TextMate grammars for Godot's shading language and other shader languages.
