name: Correct speed metrics: TTFT, prefill tok/s, decode tok/s and cache-hit % per model step
what: CodeWhale Desktop's current tok/s figure is too low because its time window includes prefill and model load. The data to fix it already exists. CodeWhale's turn.usage event carries first_token_ms, request_ms and cached-prompt tokens, and Ollama reports exact server-side timings both in its native fields and in a new `timings` block on its OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
concrete_claims: Ollama usage fields, all in nanoseconds: total_duration, load_duration, prompt_eval_count, prompt_eval_cached_count, prompt_eval_duration ('How long it took to evaluate the uncached prompt tokens'), eval_count, eval_duration. When streaming they arrive only in the final chunk with done=true (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api/usage.mdx, https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/api/types.go). The OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint maps prompt_eval_cached_count to usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and supports stream_options.include_usage. It also attaches a llama.cpp-style `timings` object {prompt_n, prompt_ms, prompt_per_token_ms, prompt_per_second, predicted_n, predicted_ms, predicted_per_token_ms, predicted_per_second} to the finish chunk (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/openai/openai.go ToTimings; https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/middleware/openai.go). A third-party write-up says this block has been there since 0.35.1 (https://dev.to/lognebudo/four-numbers-ollama-040-gives-you-now-and-which-ones-to-trust-3m80); the latest release is v0.40.3, 11 Oct 2026 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases). Known bug: prompt_per_second divides the total prompt (cached tokens included) by the uncached-only time, so it is inflated by the cache-hit ratio. The issue's example gives 3875 tok/s instead of 125. The fix, PR #18964, was still open on 12 Oct 2026 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18964). Compute it yourself as (prompt_n − cached_tokens)/prompt_ms. predicted_per_second is not affected. On the CodeWhale side, the TurnUsage event has usage{input_tokens, output_tokens, prompt_cache_hit_tokens, reasoning_tokens}, duration_ms, first_token_ms and request_ms (crates/protocol/src/event_msg.rs and crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop/model_step.rs in https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale). CodeWhale already sends stream_options.include_usage=true (crates/tui/src/client/chat.rs). Its TUI exposes `ttft` and `output_rate` status items (config.example.toml [tui].status_items).
how_we_use_it: Fix src/store/threads.ts, case 'turn.usage'. Today it computes tokPerSec = output_tokens/(duration_ms/1000), and duration_ms includes TTFT and model load. Change it to decode = output_tokens/((request_ms − first_token_ms)/1000), prefill ≈ (input_tokens − prompt_cache_hit_tokens)/(first_token_ms/1000), and cacheHit = prompt_cache_hit_tokens/input_tokens. Show four chips per model step in components/chat/Turn.tsx: TTFT, prefill tok/s, decode tok/s, cache %. Show a rolling median in layout/StatusBar.tsx. Mark the first step after a model switch as 'cold'. For exact server numbers there are two routes. (a) Upstream PR to CodeWhale: parse the `timings` block in crates/tui/src/client/chat.rs and add optional server_prompt_ms and server_predicted_ms to TurnUsage. (b) Point CodeWhale's ollama base_url at a small pass-through proxy in src-tauri/src/ollama.rs that forwards to :11434 and reads `timings` and `usage` from the final SSE chunk. Either way, apply the cached-token correction and never display Ollama's prompt_per_second as-is. A low cache % in long agent loops tells the user the prompt prefix is changing and every step re-prefills the whole context.
date: Ollama timings block: per third-party report since v0.35.1 (Sep 2026); PR #18964 opened 2026-10-12; Ollama v0.40.3 released 2026-10-11

name: Context-overflow and CPU-offload guard (silent Ollama truncation detection)
what: Agent loops with local models often fail for two silent reasons. (1) Ollama truncates chat history by default when the prompt exceeds the loaded num_ctx, so the model forgets earlier tool results and starts repeating itself. (2) The model is partly offloaded to CPU, which cuts speed several-fold. Ollama's /api/ps exposes size, size_vram and context_length, so both can be detected cheaply.
concrete_claims: /api/ps returns per model: name, model, size, digest, details, expires_at, size_vram ('VRAM usage in bytes') and context_length ('Context length for the running model') (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/api/types.go ProcessModelResponse; https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/openapi.yaml). The FAQ shows the PROCESSOR column as '100% GPU', '100% CPU' or '48%/52% CPU/GPU' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/faq.mdx). ChatRequest has `truncate` ('truncates the chat history messages if the rendered prompt exceeds the context length limit') and `shift` (api/types.go). The server defaults both to true when they are unset: `req.Truncate == nil || *req.Truncate` and `Shift: req.Shift == nil || *req.Shift` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/server/routes.go). The OpenAI-compatible request type has no truncate or shift fields at all (openai/openai.go), so /v1 clients like CodeWhale always get the defaults. chatPrompt 'truncates any messages that exceed the context window… always include 1) the latest message and 2) system messages' and logs this only at slog.Debug 'truncating input messages which exceed context length' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/server/prompt.go). Preload: an empty request to /api/chat or /api/generate loads the model, and keep_alive / OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE control residency, with a default of 5 minutes (faq.mdx). OLLAMA_LOAD_TIMEOUT is 'How long to allow model loads to stall before giving up (default "5m")' (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/envconfig/config.go). Windows logs are under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\server.log, and OLLAMA_DEBUG=1 turns on verbose logging (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.mdx).
how_we_use_it: src-tauri/src/ollama.rs ollama_status already fetches /api/ps. Have it return offloadPct = 1 − size_vram/size and contextLength for each loaded model. In the UI: (1) Show an amber 'CPU offload 37%' chip in StatusBar whenever size_vram < size, with a one-click 'try smaller num_ctx' action that reuses the existing ollama_create_variant. (2) On every turn.usage, compare usage.input_tokens with /api/ps context_length. Above about 95%, show a red banner: 'Ollama dropped old messages from the prompt; the model can no longer see earlier tool output'. Also compare CodeWhale's own ContextUsage.window_tokens (src/lib/types.ts) with context_length. If CodeWhale assumes a bigger window than Ollama actually loaded, CodeWhale's compaction never fires and Ollama truncates silently. Offer to fix either side: bake num_ctx with a variant, or lower the CodeWhale window. (3) Prewarm the selected model with an empty /api/chat request and keep_alive when a thread opens, then show load time measured by wall clock. (4) Add a 'Diagnostics' button that opens %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\server.log filtered for 'truncating input messages' (visible only with OLLAMA_DEBUG=1) and for layer-offload lines.

name: GPU telemetry via NVML (nvml-wrapper) + Windows PDH shared-memory counters for sysmem-fallback detection
what: Replace spawning nvidia-smi on every poll with in-process NVML through the nvml-wrapper crate. Add the signals that explain slowdowns: power, SM clock, throttle reasons, PCIe. On Windows, add PDH 'GPU Process Memory' counters, because NVML cannot report per-process VRAM under WDDM. Those counters also catch the driver's silent spill of VRAM into system RAM.
concrete_claims: The nvml-wrapper crate is at 0.13.0, updated 2026-08-31 (https://crates.io/crates/nvml-wrapper). It loads NVML at runtime through libloading, so on machines without NVML Nvml::init just returns an error. The README advises calling init once and storing the instance (https://github.com/Cldfire/nvml-wrapper). Relevant Device methods: memory_info, utilization_rates, power_usage, total_energy_consumption, temperature, clock_info, performance_state, pcie_throughput, current_throttle_reasons. ThrottleReasons flags include SW_POWER_CAP, HW_SLOWDOWN, SW_THERMAL_SLOWDOWN, HW_THERMAL_SLOWDOWN and HW_POWER_BRAKE_SLOWDOWN (nvml-wrapper/src/device.rs and src/bitmasks/device.rs). nvidia-smi --query-gpu fallback fields: power.draw.instant, power.draw.average, clocks.sm, clocks.max.sm, pstate, utilization.memory, pcie.link.gen.current, pcie.link.width.current, clocks_event_reasons.active ('Bitmask of active clock event reasons'), clocks_event_reasons.sw_power_cap and .hw_thermal_slowdown; clocks_throttle_reasons.* are aliases (https://gist.github.com/sansmoraxz/8a98d987f12d7edc983d611b8326fc67). NVIDIA's nvmlProcessInfo_t docs say that under WDDM usedGpuMemory is always NVML_VALUE_NOT_AVAILABLE because Windows KMD manages memory (https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/structnvmlProcessInfo__t.html). PDH counters '\GPU Process Memory(pid_…_luid_…)\Dedicated Usage' and '\Shared Usage', and '\GPU Adapter Memory(*)\Shared Usage', are readable with Get-Counter (https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/windows-get-amount-of-shared-vram-used-and-total-from-command-line/302642). Microsoft warns these counters can report incorrect values on some Windows 10 builds (https://support.microsoft.com/help/4490156). The hypomnesis crate 0.2.14 (2026-10-09) wraps PDH per-process VRAM on Windows with an nvidia-smi fallback (https://crates.io/crates/hypomnesis). Sysmem fallback: NVIDIA Control Panel → Manage 3D Settings → 'CUDA - Sysmem Fallback Policy' → 'Prefer No Sysmem Fallback', which can be set per program. Secondary sources date the spill behaviour to driver 536.40 and up (https://docs.cognex.com/deep-learning_400/web/EN/deep-learning/Content/Topics/optimization/gpu-disable-shared.htm, https://runaihome.com/blog/shared-gpu-memory-slow-local-ai-sysmem-fallback-fix-2026/).
how_we_use_it: In src-tauri/src/system.rs, replace the per-call nvidia-smi spawn in gpu_stats, which today queries 5 fields with a 4-second timeout, with a lazily initialised Nvml held in Tauri state, and keep nvidia-smi as the fallback. Every 1–2 seconds while a turn runs, emit util, memUtil, VRAM, power in watts, SM clock vs max, temperature and active throttle reasons. Draw sparklines in the GPU panel. Show chips such as 'Thermal throttle' or 'Power cap', plus 'GPU idle while turn is running', which points to a hang or a CPU-bound offload. On Windows, read PDH Shared Usage for the Ollama runner process. If it is above zero while dedicated VRAM is near total, show 'VRAM spilled to system RAM (sysmem fallback): expect 5–10× slower', with a guide to setting 'Prefer No Sysmem Fallback' for ollama.exe and a suggestion to cut num_ctx or the quant. Join decode tok/s with power to show tok/s per watt in the benchmark view.

name: Loop / hang watchdog for model loops (repetition detection, stuck patterns, turn budgets)
what: Small and quantized local models often get stuck: repeated identical tool calls, a text chunk repeated over and over, endless 'Wait…' reasoning, or a stalled stream. Gemini CLI and the OpenHands SDK ship tested heuristics for this. CodeWhale already has opt-in step, wall-clock and stream-idle budgets that the Desktop can set.
concrete_claims: Gemini CLI loopDetectionService defaults: TOOL_CALL_LOOP_THRESHOLD=5 identical consecutive calls (sha256 of name+args), CONTENT_LOOP_THRESHOLD=10 repeats of a CONTENT_CHUNK_SIZE=50-character chunk, code fences excluded, MAX_HISTORY_LENGTH=5000. An LLM-judge check runs after LLM_CHECK_AFTER_TURNS=30 turns, every 5–15 turns, with LLM_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.9 (https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts). The OpenHands SDK StuckDetector covers five scenarios: same action and observation, same action and error, monologue, alternating pattern, and context-window-error loop. Default thresholds are action_observation=4, action_error=3, monologue=3, alternating_pattern=6, scanned over the last 20 events since the last user message (https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py, .../conversation/types.py). CodeWhale settings: [tui] max_model_steps, uncapped by default, 1–100000; turn_wall_clock_secs, 30–86400; env overrides CODEWHALE_MAX_MODEL_STEPS, CODEWHALE_TURN_WALL_CLOCK_SECS and CODEWHALE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS (config.example.toml, crates/tui/src/config/subagent_limits.rs, crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_budget.rs in https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale). Research: 'Wait, Wait, Wait… Why Do Reasoning Models Loop?' reports that looping is common at low temperature and that distilled students loop far more than their teachers (arXiv 2512.12895, Dec 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12895). Qwen3 model-card guidance: do not use greedy decoding, and set presence_penalty between 0 and 2 (1.5 suggested) for 'endless repetitions' (mirror: https://friendli.ai/models/Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-FP8). Ollama's Options accept repeat_penalty, repeat_last_n, presence_penalty and frequency_penalty (api/types.go). The Modelfile documents repeat_penalty, default 1.0 (disabled), and repeat_last_n, default 64 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/modelfile.mdx).
how_we_use_it: Add src/lib/watchdog.ts and feed it from the event switch in src/store/threads.ts. (1) On item.delta for message and reasoning text, hash 50-character chunks outside code fences and flag 10 repeats. (2) On item.started/completed for tool items, hash name+args and flag 5 identical consecutive calls, or the same call failing 3 times in a row (OpenHands action_error=3). (3) Stall: no stream.progress or item.delta for N seconds while activeTurnId is set and GPU util from item 3 is about 0. On a trigger, show a non-modal bar: 'Model looks stuck in a loop' with buttons Stop (the existing POST /v1/threads/{id}/turns/{turn_id}/interrupt), Nudge (send 'You are repeating X; try a different approach'), and Retry with anti-loop preset. The preset uses ollama_create_variant to bake presence_penalty 1.5 / repeat_penalty 1.1 and a temperature of at least 0.6 into a '-antiloop' variant, because CodeWhale does not send penalty parameters. In Settings, add a 'Local model safety' section that writes max_model_steps (e.g. 150) and turn_wall_clock_secs, and sets CODEWHALE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS on the sidecar process in src-tauri/src/runtime.rs. Log every trigger per model so the A/B scorecard (item 6) can show a 'loop rate'.
date: Gemini CLI and OpenHands SDK main as of 2026-10-13; arXiv 2512.12895 (Dec 2025)

name: Built-in local eval runner: CodeWhale exec over fixture tasks (polyglot exercises + Godot shader suite) with pass@1 / pass^k
what: Let users measure which local model and settings actually finish tasks in their own agent, not on a public leaderboard. The runner drives headless `codewhale exec --auto --output-format stream-json` over small fixture tasks, each with a verifier command, and records success, steps, tokens, time, tool errors and loops. Run k times per task to measure reliability.
concrete_claims: CodeWhale headless mode: `codewhale exec --auto --output-format stream-json "fix the failing test"`. --model and --provider can go before or after exec, and --json emits a summary (crates/cli/src/lib.rs and README in https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale). CodeWhale's docs/SKILL_EVALUATION.md prescribes the method: fixed provider, model, tools and fixtures; measure task success first, then tool errors, interruptions, tokens, cache hits and time; separate dev tasks from held-out tasks; use repeated paired runs. Aider polyglot-benchmark: Exercism exercises in 6 languages, 225 in total (cpp 26, go 39, java 47, javascript 49, python 34, rust 30, counted from the repo tree). Each has .docs/instructions.md, a stub and tests; the exercises are © Exercism under Exercism's licenses (https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark). The Aider harness reports pass_rate_1 and pass_rate_2 (https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/benchmark/README.md). τ-bench defines pass^k as the probability that all k i.i.d. trials succeed. It found gpt-4o pass^8 below 25% in retail, and that consistency differs from pass@k (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.12045).
how_we_use_it: Add an 'Evals' screen under src/components/screens. A task pack is a folder of {task.toml: prompt, fixture dir, verify command, timeout}. Bundle (a) about 20 polyglot exercises in Rust and Python as a starter pack (download on demand; keep the Exercism attribution) and (b) a 'Godot shaders' pack whose verify command is the user's existing shader compile-check script. A Rust command in src-tauri/src/runtime.rs copies each fixture to a temp dir and runs the codewhale sidecar binary with exec --auto --output-format stream-json --model <m> and CODEWHALE_MAX_MODEL_STEPS / CODEWHALE_TURN_WALL_CLOCK_SECS caps. It parses the NDJSON for usage and tool errors, runs the verifier, and stores rows in a local SQLite or JSONL file. Results view: a model × task matrix with pass@1, pass^3, median wall time, decode tok/s, loop-watchdog hits, and a 'compare to last run' diff. Include Ollama settings (num_ctx, quant, KV type) in the run key so users can see whether, say, q4_K_M at 16k beats q8_0 at 8k on their own tasks.

name: A/B model comparison inside real threads (fork + per-thread model + Elo leaderboard)
what: Add a 'Compare with…' action on any turn. It forks the conversation at that turn, switches the fork to model B, replays the same prompt, and shows both runs side by side with their metrics. The user picks a winner, and wins accumulate into a personal Elo or Bradley-Terry leaderboard per task category. This is the Open WebUI arena pattern applied to a coding agent.
concrete_claims: The CodeWhale runtime HTTP API has POST /v1/threads/{id}/fork; POST /v1/threads/{id}/fork-at-turn ({"turn_id"}, which keeps that turn and drops later ones); POST /v1/threads/{id}/retry ({"depth": N, "prompt"}, which forks with the last N turns removed and immediately starts a new turn); and PATCH /v1/threads/{id} with "model". ThreadForkParams also carries model, model_provider and cwd. thread.forked events include source_thread_id (docs/RUNTIME_API.md and crates/protocol/src/lib.rs in https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale). Open WebUI's evaluation feature has an 'Arena Model' that 'randomly selects from a pool of available models' for blind comparison. Only ratings with a sibling response from a different model affect the ranking, and the Admin leaderboard is 'ranked using an Elo rating system', with a per-model activity chart (https://github.com/open-webui/docs/blob/main/docs/features/administration/evaluation/index.mdx, https://docs.openwebui.com/features/administration/evaluation/).
how_we_use_it: Add a 'Compare with…' menu item in components/chat/Turn.tsx that calls fork-at-turn on the previous turn, PATCHes the fork's model to B, and re-posts the original prompt. For turns that edit files, create a git worktree for B and pass it as the fork cwd so the two runs never touch the same files. Render a split view with both transcripts and a strip of metrics from item 1 (TTFT, decode tok/s, steps, tokens, files changed, verifier pass if configured). Offer an optional 'blind' mode that hides model names until the user votes. Store votes locally as {category, modelA, modelB, winner, settings}. Show the leaderboard on the Models screen with Elo per category, for example 'godot-shader', 'rust', 'refactor'. Use it to suggest a default model per workspace.
date: CodeWhale runtime API main 2026-10-13; Open WebUI docs main 2026-10

name: Local tracing with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (built-in store + optional OTLP export to Phoenix / otel-desktop-viewer)
what: The Desktop already receives every app-server event, so it can emit standard OTel GenAI spans and metrics without any change to CodeWhale. Use one span per turn (invoke_agent), one per model call (chat/inference) and one per tool call (execute_tool). Keep a local trace store by default and offer optional export to a self-hosted viewer.
concrete_claims: The GenAI semantic conventions have moved out of open-telemetry/semantic-conventions into a dedicated repo (https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/README.md → https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai). Everything there has status Development. Metrics include gen_ai.client.operation.duration (s), gen_ai.client.inference.duration, gen_ai.client.inference.time_to_first_chunk, gen_ai.client.inference.time_per_output_chunk, the token counters gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens / output_tokens / cache_read.input_tokens / reasoning.output_tokens, gen_ai.invoke_agent.duration, gen_ai.invoke_agent.tool_calls and gen_ai.execute_tool.duration. The span attribute is gen_ai.response.time_to_first_chunk. gen_ai.input.messages and gen_ai.output.messages are Opt-In (docs/gen-ai/client-inference.md, gen-ai-metrics.md, gen-ai-token-metrics.md, gen-ai-agent-spans.md). Rust crates: opentelemetry_sdk 0.33.1 and opentelemetry-otlp 0.33.1 (2026-10-09), tracing-opentelemetry 0.34.0 (2026-09-23) (https://crates.io/crates/opentelemetry-otlp). Arize Phoenix: `pip install arize-phoenix && phoenix serve` or `uvx arize-phoenix serve`. It stores data in SQLite under ~/.phoenix or PHOENIX_WORKING_DIR, takes OTLP HTTP at :6006/v1/traces and gRPC at :4317, and since 15.10.0 (2026-05-15) auto-converts gen_ai.* attributes to OpenInference. The latest release is v20.21.2, 13 Oct 2026 (https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix, https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/blob/main/docs/phoenix/release-notes/05-2026/05-15-2026-otel-semconv-conversion.mdx). otel-desktop-viewer ships a Windows zip with an exe, UI at localhost:8000 and OTLP on 4317/4318. It uses DuckDB in memory, or a file with --db (2 GB cap) (https://github.com/CtrlSpice/otel-desktop-viewer). Self-hosted Langfuse v4 needs six containers: langfuse:4, langfuse-worker:4, clickhouse-server:25.12, MinIO, redis:7 and postgres:17. The latest release is v4.58.0, 13 Oct 2026 (https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/main/docker-compose.yml, https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/releases).
how_we_use_it: In src-tauri, add a tracing module fed by the same SSE event stream that api.rs already proxies. Map turn.started/completed to an invoke_agent span, each turn.usage to a chat span with gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.* and time_to_first_chunk, and tool item.started/completed/failed to execute_tool spans. Always write them to a local SQLite trace store that powers a 'Timeline' tab: waterfall per turn, slowest tools, tokens per step. Add a Settings toggle 'Export OTLP to…' with a default of http://localhost:6006/v1/traces for Phoenix, plus a 'Launch Phoenix' helper that runs `uvx arize-phoenix serve` when uv is present, or otel-desktop-viewer.exe for a no-Python option. Message content stays off unless the user opts in, matching the convention's Opt-In status for gen_ai.input/output.messages. Do not recommend Langfuse for a single-GPU desktop: it needs ClickHouse, MinIO, Redis and Postgres.

name: One-click model micro-benchmark (Ollama cmd/bench methodology: warmup, epochs, exact prompt sizes, VRAM)
what: Add a reproducible 'Benchmark this model' action that measures load time, prefill tok/s and decode tok/s at several exact context sizes. It also records VRAM and GPU offload for each installed model or num_ctx variant, so users can choose the largest context that still runs 100% on GPU.
concrete_claims: Ollama ships a benchmark tool in its repo, cmd/bench (`go run ./cmd/bench -model gemma3 -epochs 6 -format csv`). It does warmup before timed epochs, tracks TTFT per epoch, tracks VRAM and CPU memory through running-process info, and outputs benchstat or CSV. `-prompt-tokens N` makes every request exactly N prompt tokens as the server counts them, chat template included. The README notes that replay may reuse prefixes and that cached_input_tokens should be inspected (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/cmd/bench/README.md). Native fields for the calculation: load_duration, prompt_eval_count, prompt_eval_cached_count, prompt_eval_duration (uncached only), eval_count and eval_duration (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api/usage.mdx). Server settings that change results: OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION, OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE ('default: f16'), OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH and OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL, default 1 (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/envconfig/config.go).
how_we_use_it: Add a Tauri command ollama_bench(model, sizes=[2k, 8k, 16k, 32k], epochs=3) in src-tauri/src/ollama.rs. It sends a cold empty-prompt load (wall-clock load time), one warmup, then timed /api/chat requests with stream=true. Each request uses a unique prompt prefix so the cache cannot inflate prefill numbers. Read prefill = (prompt_eval_count − prompt_eval_cached_count)/prompt_eval_duration and decode = eval_count/eval_duration. Sample /api/ps size_vram and NVML power during each run. Results show as a card on the Models screen: a table by context size, an offload % warning, and tok/s per watt. A 'Recommend' button picks the largest num_ctx with 100% GPU and acceptable decode speed and creates that variant with the existing ollama_create_variant. The app also displays the current FLASH_ATTENTION and KV_CACHE_TYPE so runs are comparable.
date: Ollama main 2026-10-13

name: Tool-calling reliability smoke test (BFCL-style categories against CodeWhale's real tool catalog)
what: For a coding agent, a local model's value depends mostly on making valid, correct tool calls. Add a short in-app suite modelled on BFCL categories (simple, multiple, parallel, irrelevance, multi-turn) that runs against the exact tool schemas CodeWhale sends. Keep full BFCL as an optional deep benchmark.
concrete_claims: BFCL V4 was released on 17 Jul 2025 with a new agentic domain (web search, memory) and re-weighted overall accuracy: Agentic 40%, Multi-Turn 30%, Live 10%, Non-Live 10%, Irrelevance 10%. The latest changelog entry is 1 Oct 2025 (https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla/blob/main/berkeley-function-call-leaderboard/CHANGELOG.md). CLI: `bfcl generate --model MODEL --test-category CAT --backend {vllm|sglang}`, `--skip-server-setup` for an already-running server, REMOTE_OPENAI_BASE_URL / REMOTE_OPENAI_API_KEY for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, `bfcl evaluate … --partial-eval`, `pip install bfcl-eval` with BFCL_PROJECT_ROOT (https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla/tree/main/berkeley-function-call-leaderboard). CodeWhale's TurnComplete event includes `tool_catalog`, the serialized tools sent with the turn's model request (crates/protocol/src/event_msg.rs in https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale). Ollama's /v1/chat/completions accepts `tools` (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/openai/openai.go).
how_we_use_it: Capture tool_catalog from the latest turn.completed and cache it per CodeWhale version. Ship about 30 prompts: 'read file X' (simple), choose among similar tools (multiple), 'read A and B' (parallel), 'what is 2+2' where no tool is expected (irrelevance), and 3-step chains (multi-turn, with simulated tool results). Send them straight to Ollama /v1/chat/completions with those tools. Score parse-valid JSON, schema-valid arguments, the correct tool, and false-call rate. Show a 'Tool-calling: 87%' badge per model and per num_ctx variant on the Models screen, next to the real-session tool error rate aggregated from item.failed events. Link to an advanced 'Run full BFCL' guide that sets REMOTE_OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1.
date: BFCL V4 2025-07-17 (last changelog 2025-10-01)

name: External eval harnesses as optional baselines (promptfoo, Inspect AI, mini-swe-agent + SWE-bench Verified Mini, Harbor/Terminal-Bench 2.0)
what: For users who want public-benchmark style numbers or prompt-level A/B matrices, the app can generate configs and launch maintained open-source harnesses against the local Ollama endpoint instead of reimplementing them.
concrete_claims: promptfoo's Ollama provider uses ids `ollama:chat:<model>` (/api/chat) and `ollama:completion:<model>`, with config num_predict, temperature, think, num_ctx, tools, keep_alive and passthrough, plus env OLLAMA_BASE_URL (default http://localhost:11434). Several providers in one YAML render in a single comparison table (https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/blob/main/site/docs/providers/ollama.md). The latest version is 0.124.1, 8 Oct 2026 (https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/releases). OpenAI announced its acquisition of Promptfoo on 9 Mar 2026, and the project says it remains MIT (https://qaskills.sh/blog/openai-promptfoo-acquisition-explained-2026). Inspect AI runs `inspect eval arc.py --model ollama/llama3.1`, with tool emulation via -M emulate_tools. It offers 200+ pre-built evals; the latest version is 0.3.279, 12 Oct 2026 (https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/blob/main/docs/providers.qmd, https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). mini-swe-agent v2 claims over 74% on SWE-bench Verified. It runs batches with `mini-extra swebench --subset verified --split test --workers 4` and handles local models through a LiteLLM registry with litellm_provider 'ollama' and LITELLM_MODEL_REGISTRY_PATH (https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent, docs/usage/swebench.md, docs/models/local_models.md). SWE-bench Verified Mini is a 50-instance subset (MariusHobbhahn/swe-bench-verified-mini) used with mini-SWE-agent through LiteLLM; Docker images are retained (https://github.com/intel/neural-compressor/pull/2563, merged 2026-09-17). Harbor is the official Terminal-Bench 2.0 harness: `harbor run --dataset terminal-bench@2.0 --agent … --model … --n-concurrent 4`, and `harbor datasets list` includes SWE-Bench and Aider Polyglot (https://github.com/laude-institute/harbor). The Aider benchmark (`./benchmark/benchmark.py NAME --model M --edit-format whole --threads 10 --exercises-dir polyglot-benchmark`, run inside Docker) last shipped a release in v0.86.0 (9 Aug), so it is less active (https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/benchmark/README.md, https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/releases).
how_we_use_it: On the Evals screen, add an 'Export' tab. 'Prompt matrix (promptfoo)' writes promptfooconfig.yaml with one ollama:chat:<model> provider per selected installed model (with num_ctx and think taken from the variant) and the user's saved prompts as tests, then launches `npx promptfoo@latest eval` and `promptfoo view` in a terminal. 'SWE-bench Verified Mini (mini-swe-agent)' writes the LiteLLM registry JSON and the command line, and warns about the Docker Desktop/WSL2 and disk requirements. 'Inspect' exports `--model ollama/<model>`. These are explicitly secondary to the built-in runner (item 5), which tests the actual CodeWhale agent. Treat them as external baselines and import their result files into the same results matrix when possible.
